title.zh: 卷十三 列傳第三 宋宗室及諸王上
title.en: Volume 13 Biographies 3: Members of the Song Imperial Family 1
title.raw: 卷十三 列傳第三 宋宗室及諸王上 Volume 13 Biographies 3: Members of the Song Imperial Family 1

sentences.zh: 列傳第三宋宗室及諸王上

translations.literal: Biographies 3: Song Imperial Family and Princes 1
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 3 — Members of the Song Imperial Family 1

sentences.zh: 長沙景王道憐臨川烈武王道規營浦侯遵考武帝諸子

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Changsha, Dao Lin; Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan, Dao Gui; Marquis Zunkao of Yingpu; sons of Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Changsha, Dao Lin; Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan, Dao Gui; Marquis Zunkao of Yingpu; the sons of Emperor Wu

sentences.zh: 長沙景王道憐，宋武帝中弟也。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Changsha, Dao Lin, was the middle younger brother of Emperor Wu of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Changsha, Dao Lin, was Emperor Wu of Song's next younger brother.

sentences.zh: 謝琰為徐州，命為從事史。

translations.literal: When Xie Yan was governor of Xuzhou, he appointed him an attendant officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Yan served as governor of Xuzhou, he made Dao Lin an attendant officer on his staff.

sentences.zh: 武帝克京城及平建鄴，道憐常留侍太后，後以軍功封新渝縣男。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu took the capital and pacified Jianye, Dao Lin often remained to attend the Empress Dowager; later, for military merit, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wu seized the capital and pacified Jianye, Dao Lin usually stayed behind to attend the empress dowager; later, for military merit, he was enfeoffed Baron of Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 從武帝征廣固，所部獲慕容超，以功改封竟陵縣公。

translations.literal: Following the Emperor Wu in the campaign against Guanggu, his command captured Murong Chao; for this merit his fief was changed to Duke of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Emperor Wu on the Guanggu campaign, his troops captured Murong Chao, and for that feat his fief was raised to Duke of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 及討司馬休之，道憐監太尉留府事。

translations.literal: When Sima Xiuzhi was put down, Dao Lin supervised the affairs of the Grand Marshal's office left behind at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the suppression of Sima Xiuzhi, Dao Lin oversaw the affairs of the Grand Marshal's office left at the capital.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、荊州刺史，護南蠻校尉，加都督，北府文武悉配之。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, he became General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat, and Governor of Jingzhou, Protector of the Southern Barbarians, with added overall command; all Northern Headquarters civil and military officers were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling fell, he was made General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, governor of Jingzhou, Protector of the Southern Barbarians, and overall commander; every civil and military officer of the Northern Headquarters was placed under him.

sentences.zh: 道憐素無才能，言音甚楚，舉止多諸鄙拙，畜聚常若不足。

translations.literal: Dao Lin by nature had no talent; his speech was very Chu in accent, and his bearing was mostly crude and awkward; his hoarding always seemed insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Lin had no real ability. He spoke with a thick Chu accent, his manners were mostly coarse and clumsy, and he always seemed to be scraping together more than he could keep.

sentences.zh: 去鎮日，府庫為空。

translations.literal: On the day he left his post, the treasury was empty.
translations.idiomatic: The day he left his post, the prefectural treasury stood empty.

sentences.zh: 徵拜司空、徐兗二州刺史，加都督，出鎮京口。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Grand Minister of Works and Governor of Xu and Yan provinces, with added overall command, and went out to garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled, appointed Grand Minister of Works and governor of Xu and Yan, given overall command, and sent to garrison Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，遷太尉，封長沙王。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu received the Mandate, Dao Lin was transferred to Grand Marshal and enfeoffed Prince of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu accepted the throne, Dao Lin was promoted to Grand Marshal and enfeoffed Prince of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 先是，廬陵王義真為揚州刺史，太后謂上曰：「道憐汝布衣兄弟，宜用為揚州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince Yizhen of Luling was Governor of Yangzhou. The Empress Dowager said to the Emperor, "Dao Lin is your brother from common cloth — he ought to be made Governor of Yangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Yizhen of Luling had been governor of Yangzhou. The empress dowager told the emperor, "Dao Lin is your brother from the days before you wore the dragon robe — he should be given Yangzhou."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「寄奴於道憐，豈有所惜。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Would Jitu ever begrudge Dao Lin anything?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Would I, Jitu, begrudge Dao Lin anything?"

sentences.zh: 揚州根本所寄，事務至重，非道憐所了。

translations.literal: Yangzhou is where the root of the realm is entrusted; its affairs are weightiest in the extreme — Dao Lin cannot manage them.
translations.idiomatic: "But Yangzhou is the root of the realm; its business is far too heavy for Dao Lin to handle."

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「道憐年五十，豈不如十歲兒邪？

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Dao Lin is fifty years old — is he not better than a ten-year-old child?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Dao Lin is fifty — surely he is more capable than a ten-year-old child?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「車士雖為刺史，事無大小，皆由寄奴。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Though Che Shi holds the governorship, great and small affairs all pass through Jitu.
translations.idiomatic: "Even if Che Shi holds the governorship," the emperor said, "every matter, large or small, still passes through me."

sentences.zh: 道憐年長，不親其事，於聽望不足。

translations.literal: Dao Lin is advanced in years and does not personally handle affairs — this would fall short in public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: "Dao Lin is old and would not manage things himself — the appointment would look bad."

sentences.zh: 」太后乃無言，竟不授。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then said nothing; in the end the post was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager fell silent, and in the end the appointment was never made.

sentences.zh: 道憐子義欣嗣，位豫州刺史，鎮壽陽，境內畏服，道不拾遺，遂為盛藩強鎮。

translations.literal: Dao Lin's son Yi Xin succeeded him, held the post of Governor of Yu Province, and garrisoned Shouyang; within his jurisdiction people feared and obeyed him, lost articles were not picked up, and the region became a flourishing strong frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Lin's son Yi Xin succeeded him, served as governor of Yu and garrisoned Shouyang. People within his jurisdiction feared and respected him; things dropped on the road were not picked up, and the region became a flourishing, powerful frontier command.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰成王。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted an office equal to the Three Excellencies; his posthumous title was Prince Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously granted an office equal to the Three Excellencies and given the posthumous title Prince Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子悼王瑾嗣，傳爵至子，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Dao Jin, succeeded; the title passed to his son; when Qi received the Mandate, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Dao Jin, succeeded; the title passed to the next generation, and when Qi took the throne the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 韞弟述字彥思，亦甚庸劣。

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother Shu, styled Yansi, was likewise very mediocre and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's younger brother Shu, styled Yansi, was equally mediocre and dull.

sentences.zh: 從子俁疾危篤，父彥節母蕭對之泣，述嘗候之，便命左右取酒肉令俁進之，皆莫知其意。

translations.literal: His nephew Hou was gravely ill; Hou's father Yanjie and mother Xiao wept over him. Shu once visited; he immediately ordered attendants to bring wine and meat and had Hou eat — none knew his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Hou lay gravely ill; Hou's father Yanjie and mother Xiao wept at his bedside. When Shu came to visit, he at once ordered attendants to bring wine and meat and made Hou eat — no one understood why.

sentences.zh: 或問焉，答曰：「禮雲，有疾飲酒食肉。

translations.literal: When some asked, he answered, "The Rites say: when ill, one may drink wine and eat meat."
translations.idiomatic: Asked to explain, he said, "The Rites say that when one is ill one may drink wine and eat meat."

sentences.zh: 」述又嘗新有緦慘，或詣之，問其母安否。

translations.literal: Shu also once had fresh mourning garb; someone called on him and asked whether his mother was well.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was once in fresh mourning dress when a visitor asked after his mother's health.

sentences.zh: 述曰：「惟有愁惛。

translations.literal: Shu said, "There is only sorrow and confusion."
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied, "Only sorrow and confusion."

sentences.zh: 」次訪其子，對曰：「所謂父子聚麀。

translations.literal: Next he was asked about his son; he answered, "What is called father and son sharing a doe."
translations.idiomatic: Asked next about his son, he answered, "What people call father and son sharing a doe."

sentences.zh: 」蓋謂麀為憂也。

translations.literal: It was said he meant doe as sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: He apparently meant "doe" as "sorrow."

sentences.zh: 義欣弟義融封桂陽縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Yi Xin's younger brother Yi Rong was enfeoffed Marquis of Guiyang with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Xin's younger brother Yi Rong was enfeoffed Marquis of Guiyang, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 凡王子為侯，食邑皆千戶。

translations.literal: Whenever imperial princes became marquises, their fiefs were all one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an imperial prince was enfeoffed as a marquis, the fief was always one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 義融位五兵尚書，領軍，有質幹，善於用短楯。

translations.literal: Yi Rong held the post of Minister of the Five Armies and Commander of the Palace Guard; he had solid substance and was skilled with the short shield.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Rong served as Minister of the Five Armies and commander of the palace guard. He had solid substance and was skilled with the short shield.

sentences.zh: 卒諡恭侯。

translations.literal: At death his posthumous title was Marquis Gong.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he received the posthumous title Marquis Gong.

sentences.zh: 子孝侯覬嗣，無子，弟襲以子晃繼。

translations.literal: His son, Marquis Xiao Ji, succeeded; having no son, his younger brother Xi had his son Huang succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Marquis Xiao Ji, succeeded; childless, the line passed to Xi's son Huang.

sentences.zh: 襲字茂德，性庸鄙，為郢州刺史，暑月露褌上聽事，時綱紀政伏合，怪之，訪問乃知是襲。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Maode, was coarse and vulgar by nature; as Governor of Yingzhou, in midsummer he wore only drawers above the reception hall. The chief clerk, Zheng Fu, thought it strange, inquired, and only then learned it was Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, styled Maode, was coarse and vulgar. As governor of Yingzhou, in midsummer he appeared in the reception hall wearing only his drawers. Chief clerk Zheng Fu found it odd, made inquiries, and learned it was Xi.

sentences.zh: 義融弟義宗，幼為武帝所愛，字曰伯奴，封新渝縣侯，位太子左衛率。

translations.literal: Yi Rong's younger brother Yi Zong was loved by the Emperor Wu from childhood; he was called Bonu, enfeoffed Marquis of Xinyu, and held the post of Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Rong's younger brother Yi Zong was cherished by Emperor Wu from childhood. Called Bonu, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xinyu and served as Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.

sentences.zh: 坐門生杜德靈放橫打人，入義宗第蔽隱，免官。

translations.literal: He was removed from office because his student Du Deling acted violently and beat people, then entered Yi Zong's residence and was hidden there.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed because his student Du Deling had beaten people violently and then taken refuge in Yi Zong's residence, where Yi Zong concealed him.

sentences.zh: 德靈以姿色，故義宗愛寵之。

translations.literal: Deling was favored and cherished by Yi Zong because of his good looks.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his handsome looks, Deling was Yi Zong's favorite.

sentences.zh: 義宗卒于南兗州刺史，諡曰惠侯。

translations.literal: Yi Zong died while Governor of Southern Yanzhou; his posthumous title was Marquis Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Zong died while serving as governor of Southern Yanzhou and received the posthumous title Marquis Hui.

sentences.zh: 子懷珍嗣，無子，弟彥節以子承繼。

translations.literal: His son Huai Zhen succeeded; having no son, his younger brother Yanjie had his son Cheng succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huai Zhen succeeded; childless, the line passed to Yanjie's son Cheng.

sentences.zh: 彥節少以宗室清謹見知，孝武時，其弟遐坐通嫡母殷氏養女雲敷，殷每禁之。

translations.literal: Yanjie was known from youth in the imperial clan for purity and discretion. In Emperor Xiaowu's time, his younger brother Xia was charged with relations with his stepmother Lady Yin's foster daughter Yun Fu; Yin often forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie was known from youth in the imperial clan for purity and discretion. Under Emperor Xiaowu, his younger brother Xia was charged with relations with his stepmother Lady Yin's foster daughter Yun Fu, whom Lady Yin repeatedly forbade him to see.

sentences.zh: 及殷亡，口血出，眾疑遐行毒害。

translations.literal: When Yin died, blood came from her mouth; the crowd suspected Xia of poisoning her.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Yin died, blood issued from her mouth, and many suspected Xia of poisoning her.

sentences.zh: 孝武使彥節從弟祗諷彥節啟證其事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu had Yanjie's younger cousin Zhi hint to Yanjie to memorialize and testify in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu had Yanjie's younger cousin Zhi suggest that Yanjie memorialize the throne and testify in the case.

sentences.zh: 彥節曰：「行路之人尚不應爾，今日乃可一門同盡，無容奉敕。

translations.literal: Yanjie said, "Even a passerby on the road ought not to do such a thing — how much less today may one obey an edict and destroy the whole clan together?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie said, "Even a stranger on the road would not do such a thing — how could I obey an edict and bring the whole clan to ruin?"

sentences.zh: 」眾以此稱之。

translations.literal: The crowd praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: People praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝即位，累遷尚書左僕射，參選。

translations.literal: After the Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, Yanjie was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and took part in selections for office.
translations.idiomatic: After the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Yanjie rose repeatedly to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and took part in personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 元徽元年，領吏部，加兵五百人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui he headed the Ministry of Personnel and was given five hundred additional guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhui he headed the Ministry of Personnel and was granted five hundred additional guards.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休範為逆，中領軍劉勉出守石頭，彥節權兼領軍將軍，所給加兵，自隨入殿。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Central Army Commander Liu Mian went out to hold Shitou; Yanjie temporarily held the post of Commander of the Palace Guard as well, and the extra guards given him entered the palace with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Central Army Commander Liu Mian went out to hold Shitou. Yanjie temporarily held the post of palace guard commander as well, and the extra guards assigned him entered the palace at his side.

sentences.zh: 封當陽侯，與齊高帝、袁粲、褚彥回分日入直，平決機事，遷中書令，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Marquis of Dangyang and, with Emperor Gao of Qi, Yuan Can, and Chu Yuanhui, took turns entering attendance; they jointly decided urgent affairs. He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed Marquis of Dangyang, he joined Emperor Gao of Qi, Yuan Can, and Chu Yuanhui in daily attendance at court, deciding urgent affairs together. He was made Director of the Secretariat with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 及帝廢為蒼梧王，彥節出集議，于路逢從弟韞。

translations.literal: When the emperor was deposed and made Prince Cangwu, Yanjie went out to an assembly; on the road he met his younger cousin Yun.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was deposed and made Prince Cangwu, Yanjie went out to an assembly and met his younger cousin Yun on the road.

sentences.zh: 韞問曰：「今日之事，故當歸兄邪？

translations.literal: Yun asked, "In today's affair, ought it not to fall to you, elder brother?"
translations.idiomatic: Yun asked, "In today's affair, shouldn't the leadership fall to you, elder brother?"

sentences.zh: 」彥節曰：「吾等已讓領軍矣。

translations.literal: Yanjie said, "We have already yielded to the palace guard commander."
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie said, "We have already yielded the command to the palace guard commander."

sentences.zh: 」韞捶胸曰：「兄肉中詎有血邪，今年族矣。

translations.literal: Yun beat his breast and said, "Can there be blood in elder brother's flesh? This year the clan will be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Yun struck his breast and cried, "Is there no blood in your flesh, brother? This year the whole clan will be wiped out."

sentences.zh: 」齊高帝聞而惡之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi heard of it, he detested him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi heard this, he took a deep dislike to Yun.

sentences.zh: 順帝即位，轉尚書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun ascended the throne, Yanjie was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun took the throne, Yanjie was made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時齊高帝輔政，彥節知運祚將遷，密懷異圖。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Gao of Qi was regent; Yanjie secretly knew the mandate was about to shift and harbored a separate design.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi was then regent. Yanjie sensed the mandate was shifting and secretly nursed a different plan.

sentences.zh: 及沈攸之舉兵，齊高帝入屯朝堂，袁粲鎮石頭，潛與彥節及諸大將黃回等謀夜會石頭，詰旦乃發。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi raised troops, Emperor Gao of Qi entered and encamped at the Court Hall; Yuan Can garrisoned Shitou. Secretly Yuan Can, Yanjie, and the great generals Huang Hui and others planned to meet at Shitou by night and move at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rose in arms, Emperor Gao of Qi encamped in the Court Hall while Yuan Can held Shitou. Yuan Can secretly planned with Yanjie and generals including Huang Hui to meet at Shitou by night and strike at dawn.

sentences.zh: 彥節素怯，騷擾不自安。

translations.literal: Yanjie was by nature timid; he was agitated and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie was timid by nature and grew restless and uneasy.

sentences.zh: 再晡後，便自丹陽郡車載婦女，盡室奔石頭。

translations.literal: After the second watch he loaded his wife and women into a cart from Danyang commandery and fled with his whole household to Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: After the second watch he loaded his wife and household women into a cart from Danyang commandery and fled with his entire family to Shitou.

sentences.zh: 臨去，婦蕭氏強勸令食，彥節歠羹寫胸中，手振不自禁。

translations.literal: As he was leaving, his wife, the Lady Xiao, strongly urged him to eat; Yanjie drank soup that spilled on his chest, and his hands shook uncontrollably.
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving, his wife Lady Xiao pressed him to eat. Yanjie drank soup that spilled down his chest, his hands shaking beyond control.

sentences.zh: 其主簿丁靈衛聞難即入，語左右曰：「今日之事，難以取濟。

translations.literal: His chief clerk Ding Lingwei, hearing of the crisis, entered at once and said to those around him, "Today's affair will be hard to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk Ding Lingwei, hearing of the crisis, entered at once and told those around him, "Today's affair will be hard to succeed.

sentences.zh: 但我受劉公厚恩，義無二情。

translations.literal: But I have received great kindness from Lord Liu and cannot be of two minds."
translations.idiomatic: But I have received great kindness from Lord Liu and owe him undivided loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」及至見粲，粲驚曰：「何遽便來，事今敗矣。

translations.literal: When he arrived and saw Yuan Can, Can said in alarm, "Why have you come so hastily? The affair is ruined now."
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Yuan Can, Can cried in alarm, "Why come so hastily? The affair is ruined already."

sentences.zh: 」彥節曰：「今得見公，萬死何恨。

translations.literal: Yanjie said, "Now that I have seen you, sir, I regret nothing though I die ten thousand deaths."
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie said, "Now that I have seen you, sir, I would die ten thousand deaths without regret."

sentences.zh: 」從弟韞直省內，與直合將軍卜伯興謀其夜共攻齊高帝，會彥節事覺，秣陵令劉實、建康令劉遐密告齊高帝，高帝夜使驍騎將軍王敬則收殺之，伯興亦遇害。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Yun was on duty inside; with Direct Attendance General Bu Boxing he plotted that night to attack Emperor Gao of Qi together. When Yanjie's affair was discovered, Moling magistrate Liu Shi and Jiankang magistrate Liu Xia secretly reported to Emperor Gao of Qi; at night the General of Fierce Cavalry Wang Jingze was sent to seize and kill them, and Boxing also perished.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Yun was on palace duty and plotted with Direct Attendance General Bu Boxing to attack Emperor Gao of Qi that same night. When Yanjie's plot was discovered, Moling magistrate Liu Shi and Jiankang magistrate Liu Xia secretly reported to Emperor Gao of Qi, who that night sent General of Fierce Cavalry Wang Jingze to seize and kill them; Boxing perished as well.

sentences.zh: 粲敗，彥節踰城走，於額簷湖見禽被殺。

translations.literal: When Yuan Can was defeated, Yanjie climbed over the wall and fled; at Eyebrow Ridge Lake he was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Can was defeated, Yanjie climbed over the wall, and fled; at Eyebrow Ridge Lake he was captured, and killed.

sentences.zh: 彥節子俁嘗賦詩云：「城上草，植根非不高，所恨風霜早。

translations.literal: Yanjie's son Hou once composed a poem saying, "Grass on the wall — its roots are not too low, but I regret the early frost and wind."
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie's son Hou once wrote a poem: "Grass on the wall — its roots are not too shallow, but I regret the early frost and wind."

sentences.zh: 」時咸雲此為祅句。

translations.literal: At the time all said this was an omen verse.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone said this was an omen verse.

sentences.zh: 事敗，俁與弟陔剃髮被法服向京口，於客舍為人識，執于建康獄盡殺之。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, Hou and his younger brother Ai shaved their heads, put on monks' robes, and went toward Jingkou; at an inn they were recognized, seized, and all were killed in Jiankang prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed, Hou and his younger brother Ai shaved their heads, donned monks' robes, and headed for Jingkou; at an inn they were recognized, seized, and all were killed in Jiankang prison.

sentences.zh: 彥節既貴，士子自非三署不得上方榻，時人以此少之。

translations.literal: Once Yanjie had risen high, scholars who were not of the Three Offices were not permitted to sit on the upper couch in his presence; people thought less of him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yanjie had risen high, scholars not of the Three Offices were not allowed the upper couch in his presence; people thought less of him for this.

sentences.zh: 其妻蕭思話女也，常懼禍敗，每謂曰：「君富貴已足，故應為兒作計。

translations.literal: His wife was the daughter of Xiao Sihua; she always feared disaster and ruin, and often said to him, "Your wealth and honor are already enough — you ought to plan for the sons."
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Xiao Sihua's daughter; she always feared disaster and often told him, "Your wealth and honor are already enough — you ought to plan for our sons."

sentences.zh: 」彥節不從，故及禍。

translations.literal: Yanjie did not listen, and therefore met with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie would not listen, and so met with calamity.

sentences.zh: 彥節弟遐字彥道，為嫡母殷暴亡，有司糾之，徙始安郡。

translations.literal: Yanjie's younger brother Xia, styled Yandao, had his stepmother Lady Yin die suddenly; the authorities impeached him and he was banished to Shi'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie's younger brother Xia, styled Yandao, was impeached when his stepmother Lady Yin died suddenly and was banished to Shi'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 後得還，位吳郡太守，至是亦見誅。

translations.literal: Later he was allowed to return and held the post of Governor of Wu commandery; at this time he too was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was allowed to return and served as governor of Wu commandery; at this time he too was executed.

sentences.zh: 遐人才甚凡，自諱名有同主諱，常對客曰：「孝武無道，見枉殺母。

translations.literal: Xia's talent was very ordinary; he avoided his own name because it matched the imperial taboo, and he often said to guests, "Emperor Xiaowu was without the Way and wrongly killed my mother."
translations.idiomatic: Xia's talent was very ordinary. Because his name matched the imperial taboo, he avoided it and often told guests, "Emperor Xiaowu was without the Way and wrongly killed my mother."

sentences.zh: 」其頑騃若此。

translations.literal: He was obstinate and dull to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: He was obstinate and dull to that degree.

sentences.zh: 及彥節當權，遐累求方伯。

translations.literal: When Yanjie held power, Xia repeatedly asked for a provincial governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yanjie held power, Xia repeatedly asked for a provincial governorship.

sentences.zh: 彥節曰：「我在事，而用汝作州，於聽望不足。

translations.literal: Yanjie said, "While I am in office, to use you as a governor would fall short in public esteem."
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie said, "While I am in office, making you a governor would look bad."

sentences.zh: 」遐曰：「富貴則言不可相關，從坐之日得免不？

translations.literal: Xia said, "When there is wealth and honor you say we cannot be connected — on the day of shared guilt, can one escape?"
translations.idiomatic: Xia said, "When there is wealth, and honor you say we cannot be connected; on the day of shared guilt, can one escape?"

sentences.zh: 「至是果死。

translations.literal: At this time he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he indeed died.

sentences.zh: 義宗弟義賓，封興安侯，位徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Yi Zong's younger brother Yi Bin was enfeoffed Marquis of Xing'an and held the post of Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Zong's younger brother Yi Bin was enfeoffed Marquis of Xing'an and served as governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰肅侯。

translations.literal: At death his posthumous title was Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he received the posthumous title Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 義賓弟義綦，封營道縣侯，凡鄙無識。

translations.literal: Yi Bin's younger brother Yi Qi was enfeoffed Marquis of Yingdao; he was vulgar and without understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Bin's younger brother Yi Qi was enfeoffed Marquis of Yingdao; he was vulgar, and without understanding.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚嘗謂曰：「陸士衡詩雲，'營道無烈心'，其何意苦阿父如此。

translations.literal: Prince Jun of Shixing once said to him, "Lu Shiheng's poem says, 'On the road to Ying there is no fierce heart' — why do you distress Uncle so?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun of Shixing once told him, "Lu Ji wrote in a poem, 'On the road to Ying there is no fierce heart' — why do you distress Uncle so?"

sentences.zh: 」義綦曰：「下官初不識士衡，何忽見苦。

translations.literal: Yi Qi said, "This humble official never knew Shiheng — why suddenly pick on me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qi said, "I never knew Lu Ji — why suddenly pick on me?"

sentences.zh: 」其庸塞皆然。

translations.literal: His mediocrity and obtuseness were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: His mediocrity and obtuseness were all of this sort.

sentences.zh: 位湘州刺史，諡僖侯。

translations.literal: He held the post of Governor of Xiangzhou; his posthumous title was Marquis Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Xiangzhou and received the posthumous title Marquis Xi.

sentences.zh: 臨川烈武王道規字道則，武帝少弟也。

translations.literal: Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan, Dao Gui, styled Daozi, was the youngest younger brother of the Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan, Dao Gui, styled Daozi, was Emperor Wu's youngest brother.

sentences.zh: 倜儻有大志，預謀誅桓玄。

translations.literal: Unconventional and bold, he had great ambition and took part in plotting the execution of Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Unconventional and bold, he nursed great ambitions and took part in plotting Huan Xuan's overthrow.

sentences.zh: 時桓弘鎮廣陵，以為征虜中兵參軍。

translations.literal: At that time Huan Hong garrisoned Guangling; Dao Gui was made Middle Army Major under the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huan Hong garrisoned Guangling; Dao Gui was made a middle army major on the staff of the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 武帝克京城，道規亦以其日與劉毅、孟昶斬弘。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu took the capital, Dao Gui on that same day joined Liu Yi and Meng Chang in beheading Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the capital, Dao Gui on that same day joined Liu Yi and Meng Chang in beheading Hong.

sentences.zh: 玄敗走，道規與劉毅、何無忌追破之。

translations.literal: When Xuan fled in defeat, Dao Gui with Liu Yi and He Wuji pursued and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan fled in defeat, Dao Gui with Liu Yi and He Wuji pursued and routed him.

sentences.zh: 無忌欲乘勝直造江陵。

translations.literal: Wuji wished to press the victory and strike straight for Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji wished to press the victory and march straight on Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 道規曰：「諸桓世居西楚，群小皆為竭力；

translations.literal: Dao Gui said, "The Huan clan has long held western Chu; the lesser men all exert themselves for them;
translations.idiomatic: Dao Gui said, "The Huans have long held western Chu; every lesser man serves them with all his strength;

sentences.zh: 桓振勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: Huan Zhen's courage tops the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Zhen's courage tops all three armies.

sentences.zh: 且可頓兵以計策縻之。

translations.literal: For now we should halt the army and use stratagem to tie them down."
translations.idiomatic: For now we should halt and use stratagem to tie them down."

sentences.zh: 」無忌不從，果為振敗。

translations.literal: Wuji did not follow; he was indeed defeated by Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji would not listen and was indeed defeated by Zhen.

sentences.zh: 乃退還尋陽，繕舟甲復進，遂平巴陵。

translations.literal: They then withdrew to Xunyang, repaired boats and armor, and advanced again, finally pacifying Baling.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew to Xunyang, repaired boats and armor, and advanced again, finally pacifying Baling.

sentences.zh: 江陵之平，道規推毅為元功，無忌為次，自居其末。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, Dao Gui ranked Yi first in merit, Wuji second, and himself last.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Dao Gui ranked Yi first in merit, Wuji second, and himself last.

sentences.zh: 以起義勳，封華容縣公，累遷領護南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: For merit in raising the righteous army, he was enfeoffed Duke of Huarong; he was repeatedly promoted to Protector of the Southern Barbarians and Governor of Jingzhou, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in raising the righteous army he was enfeoffed Duke of Huarong and rose repeatedly to Protector of the Southern Barbarians, governor of Jingzhou, and overall commander.

sentences.zh: 善於刑政，士庶畏而愛之。

translations.literal: He was skilled in penal administration; gentry and commoners feared yet loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in law and administration; gentry and commoners feared him yet loved him.

sentences.zh: 盧循寇逼建鄴，道規遣司馬王鎮之及揚武將軍檀道濟、廣武將軍到彥之等赴援朝廷，至尋陽，為循党荀林所破。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed toward Jianye, Dao Gui sent Marshal Wang Zhenzhi and Generals Who Display Martiality Tan Daoji and Who Display Valor Dao Yanzhi and others to aid the court; reaching Xunyang, they were defeated by Xun's partisan Xun Lin.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun pressed toward Jianye, Dao Gui sent Marshal Wang Zhenzhi and Generals Tan Daoji and Dao Yanzhi to aid the court; reaching Xunyang, they were defeated by Xun's partisan Xun Lin.

sentences.zh: 林乘勝伐江陵，聲言徐道覆已克建鄴。

translations.literal: Lin pressed the victory to attack Jiangling, declaring that Xu Daofu had already taken Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Lin pressed the victory toward Jiangling, declaring that Xu Daofu had already taken Jianye.

sentences.zh: 而桓謙自長安入蜀，譙縱以謙為荊州刺史，與其大將譙道福俱寇江陵。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Huan Qian entered Shu from Chang'an; Qiao Zong made Qian Governor of Jingzhou, and with his great general Qiao Daofu together pressed Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Huan Qian entered Shu from Chang'an; Qiao Zong made Qian governor of Jingzhou, and with his great general Qiao Daofu together pressed Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 道規乃會將士告之曰：「吾東來文武足以濟事，欲去者不禁。

translations.literal: Dao Gui then assembled officers and soldiers and told them, "The civil and military men I brought east are enough to succeed — whoever wishes to leave is not forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Dao Gui assembled his officers and told them, "The civil and military men I brought east are enough to win — whoever wishes to leave may go."

sentences.zh: 」因夜開城門，眾咸憚服，莫有去者。

translations.literal: That night he opened the city gates; the crowd all feared and submitted, and none left.
translations.idiomatic: That night he opened the city gates; the troops all stood in awe, and none departed.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史魯宗之自襄陽來赴，或謂宗之未可測。

translations.literal: Governor of Yongzhou Lu Zongzhi came from Xiangyang to aid; some said Zongzhi could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi, governor of Yongzhou, came from Xiangyang to aid; some said he could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 道規乃單車迎之，眾咸感悅。

translations.literal: Dao Gui then went out alone in a cart to meet him; the crowd all felt moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Gui then went out alone in a cart to meet him; the troops all felt moved and reassured.

sentences.zh: 眾議欲使檀道濟、到彥之共擊荀林等。

translations.literal: The assembly wished to send Tan Daoji and Dao Yanzhi together to strike Xun Lin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly wished to send Tan Daoji and Dao Yanzhi together against Xun Lin and the others.

sentences.zh: 道規曰：「非吾自行不決。

translations.literal: Dao Gui said, "Unless I go myself, the matter will not be decided."
translations.idiomatic: Only if he went in person, Dao Gui said, could the matter be decided.

sentences.zh: 」乃使宗之居守，委以心腹，率諸將大敗謙，斬之。

translations.literal: He then had Zongzhi remain on guard and entrusted him with his inner circle; leading the generals he greatly defeated Qian and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zongzhi remain on guard and entrusted him with his inner circle; leading the generals he routed Qian and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 諮議劉遵追荀林，斬之巴陵。

translations.literal: Counselor Liu Zun pursued Xun Lin and beheaded him at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Counselor Liu Zun pursued Xun Lin, and beheaded him at Baling.

sentences.zh: 初，謙至枝江，江陵士庶皆與謙書，言城內虛實。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qian reached Zhijiang, the gentry and commoners of Jiangling all wrote to Qian about conditions inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qian reached Zhijiang, Jiangling's gentry and commoners all wrote to Qian about conditions inside the city.

sentences.zh: 道規一皆焚燒，眾乃大安。

translations.literal: Dao Gui burned them all; the crowd then felt greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Gui burned them all; the people then felt greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 徐道覆奄至破塚，魯宗之已還襄陽，人情大震。

translations.literal: Xu Daofu suddenly arrived and broke Pozhong; Lu Zongzhi had already returned to Xiangyang, and morale was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu suddenly arrived and broke Pozhong; Lu Zongzhi had already returned to Xiangyang, and morale shook badly.

sentences.zh: 或傳循已克都，遣道覆上為刺史。

translations.literal: Some reported that Xun had already taken the capital and sent Daofu up as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Some reported that Xun had already taken the capital, and sent Daofu up as governor.

sentences.zh: 江、漢士庶感其焚書之恩，無復二志。

translations.literal: The gentry and commoners of the Jiang and Han regions, grateful for his burning the letters, had no second thought.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and commoners of the Jiang and Han regions, grateful that he had burned the letters, stood firm with him.

sentences.zh: 道規使劉遵為遊軍，自拒道覆，前驅失利。

translations.literal: Dao Gui sent Liu Zun as a mobile force to meet Daofu himself; the vanguard was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Gui sent Liu Zun as a mobile force while he himself met Daofu; the vanguard was defeated.

sentences.zh: 道規壯氣愈厲，遵自外橫擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Dao Gui's bold spirit grew fiercer; Zun struck from the flank and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Gui's fighting spirit grew fiercer; Zun struck from the flank and routed them.

sentences.zh: 初使遵為遊軍，眾咸言不宜割見力置無用之地。

translations.literal: At first, when he sent Zun as a mobile force, the crowd all said it was wrong to split visible strength and place it in useless ground.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when he sent Zun as a mobile force, everyone said it was wrong to split his strength and place it where it seemed useless.

sentences.zh: 及破道覆，果得遊軍之力，眾乃服焉。

translations.literal: When Daofu was defeated, it indeed owed to the mobile force's strength; the crowd then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Daofu was defeated, it indeed owed to the mobile force; the troops then submitted.

sentences.zh: 遵字慧明，臨淮海西人，道規從母兄也，位淮南太守，追封監利縣侯。

translations.literal: Zun, styled Huiming, was a native of Linhuai Haixi; he was Dao Gui's maternal cousin and held the post of Governor of Huainan; posthumously he was enfeoffed Marquis of Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: Zun, styled Huiming, came from Haixi in Linhuai; he was Dao Gui's maternal cousin, served as governor of Huainan, and was posthumously enfeoffed Marquis of Jianli.

sentences.zh: 九年，出為平西將軍、荊州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jingzhou, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he went out as General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Jingzhou, with overall command.

sentences.zh: 荊州居上流之重，資實兵甲居朝廷之半，故武帝諸子遍居之。

translations.literal: Jingzhou occupied the weight of the upper stream; its resources and armor were half the court's — therefore the Emperor Wu's sons all held it in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou held the weight of the upper Yangzi; its resources and armor equaled half the court's — therefore Emperor Wu's sons held it in turn.

sentences.zh: 義慶以宗室令美，故特有此授。

translations.literal: Yi Qing had fine reputation in the imperial clan and therefore received this appointment in particular.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qing enjoyed fine reputation in the imperial clan and therefore received this appointment in particular.

sentences.zh: 性謙虛，始至及去鎮，迎送物並不受。

translations.literal: By nature modest, on first arrival and on leaving his post he accepted none of the gifts of welcome and farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Modest by nature, on arrival and on leaving he accepted none of the gifts of welcome and farewell.

sentences.zh: 十二年，普使內外群臣舉士，義慶表舉前臨沮令新野庾實、前征奉朝請武陵龔祈、處士南陽師覺授。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year a general order went out for civil and military ministers to recommend scholars; Yi Qing memorialized recommending former Linju magistrate Geng Shi of Xinye, former Conferral Attendant Gong Qi of Wuling, and recluse Shi Jueshou of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the court ordered civil and military ministers to recommend scholars; Yi Qing memorialized recommending Geng Shi of Xinye, Gong Qi of Wuling, and the recluse Shi Jueshou of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 義慶留心撫物，州統內官長親老不隨在官舍者，一年聽三吏餉家。

translations.literal: Yi Qing attended to comforting the people; within the province, officials whose parents were old and not lodged in official quarters were allowed three clerks per year to supply the home.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qing attended carefully to comforting the people; within the province, officials whose elderly parents did not live in official quarters were allowed three clerks per year to supply the home.

sentences.zh: 先是，王弘為江州，亦有此制。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Hong was in Jiangzhou, there was also this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Hong held Jiangzhou, the same rule had applied.

sentences.zh: 在州八年，為西土所安。

translations.literal: During eight years in the province, the western lands were settled by him.
translations.idiomatic: During eight years in the province, the western lands were settled under him.

sentences.zh: 撰徐州先賢傳十卷奏上之。

translations.literal: He compiled Biographies of Worthies of Xuzhou in ten fascicles and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Biographies of Worthies of Xuzhou in ten fascicles and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又擬班固典引為典敘，以述皇代之美。

translations.literal: He also modeled Ban Gu's Canon Introduction as Canon Narrative to set forth the beauty of the imperial age.
translations.idiomatic: He also modeled Ban Gu's Canon Introduction as Canon Narrative to set forth the glories of the age.

sentences.zh: 改授江州，又遷南兗州刺史，並帶都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangzhou, then moved to Governor of Southern Yanzhou, both with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiangzhou, then made governor of Southern Yanzhou, both with overall command.

sentences.zh: 尋即本號加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he received his original title with an added office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he received his original title with an added office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 性簡素，寡嗜欲，愛好文義，文辭雖不多，足為宗室之表。

translations.literal: By nature simple and plain, with few desires, he loved literary meaning; though his writings were not many, he was enough to be the model of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Simple and plain by nature, with few desires, he loved letters; though his writings were not many, he was enough to be the model of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 歷任無浮淫之過；

translations.literal: In successive posts he had no licentious excess;
translations.idiomatic: Through successive appointments he showed no licentious excess;

sentences.zh: 唯晚節奉沙門頗致費損。

translations.literal: only in his later years serving Buddhist monks he incurred considerable expense.
translations.idiomatic: only in his later years, patronizing Buddhist monks, he incurred considerable expense.

sentences.zh: 少善騎乘，及長，不復跨馬，招聚才學之士，遠近必至。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at riding; when grown he no longer mounted a horse, but gathered men of talent and learning — from near and far they always came.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was skilled at riding; when grown he no longer mounted a horse but gathered men of talent and learning — from near and far they always came.

sentences.zh: 太尉袁淑文冠當時，義慶在江州請為衛軍諮議。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yuan Shu was the literary crown of the age; Yi Qing at Jiangzhou invited him as Counselor of the Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Yuan Shu's writing crowned the age; Yi Qing at Jiangzhou invited him as Counselor of the Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 其餘吳郡陸展、東海何長瑜、鮑照等，並有辭章之美，引為佐吏國臣。

translations.literal: The rest — Lu Zhan of Wu commandery, He Changyu of Donghai, Bao Zhao and others — all had beauty in their writings and were brought in as staff and household ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The rest — Lu Zhan of Wu, He Changyu of Donghai, Bao Zhao and others — all had beauty in their writings and were brought in as staff and household ministers.

sentences.zh: 所著世說十卷，撰集林二百卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: What he wrote, A New Account of Tales of the World in ten fascicles, and Collected Forests in two hundred fascicles, both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His A New Account of Tales of the World in ten fascicles and Collected Forests in two hundred fascicles both circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 文帝每與義慶書，常加意斟酌。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Wen wrote to Yi Qing, he always added careful deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Wen wrote to Yi Qing, he always weighed his words with care.

sentences.zh: 鮑照字明遠，東海人，文辭瞻逸。

translations.literal: Bao Zhao, styled Mingyuan, was a man of Donghai; his writings were brilliant and free.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zhao, styled Mingyuan, came from Donghai; his writing was brilliant and free.

sentences.zh: 嘗為古樂府，文甚遒麗。

translations.literal: He once wrote old yuefu; the text was very forceful and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote old yuefu lyrics; the text was very forceful and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，河濟俱清，當時以為美瑞。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era the Yellow and Ji rivers both ran clear; at the time this was taken as an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era the Yellow, and Ji rivers both ran clear; at the time this was taken as an auspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 照為河清頌，其序甚工。

translations.literal: Zhao wrote an Ode to the River's Clarity; its preface was very skilled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao wrote an Ode to the River's Clarity. its preface was very skilled.

sentences.zh: 照始嘗謁義慶未見知，欲貢詩言志，人止之曰：「卿位尚卑，不可輕忤大王。

translations.literal: At first Zhao once called on Yi Qing and was not recognized; he wished to present poems to express his intent, but people stopped him, saying, "Your rank is still low — you must not lightly offend the prince."
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhao called on Yi Qing and was not recognized; he wished to present poems to declare his intent, but people stopped him, saying, "Your rank is still low — you must not lightly offend the prince."

sentences.zh: 」照勃然曰：「千載上有英才異士沈沒而不聞者，安可數哉。

translations.literal: Zhao said angrily, "Above in a thousand years are talented and unusual men who sink and are not heard — can one count them?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said angrily, "Above in a thousand years are talented and unusual men who sink unheard — can one count them?

sentences.zh: 大丈夫豈可遂蘊智慧，使蘭艾不辨，終日碌碌，與燕雀相隨乎。

translations.literal: How can a great man hoard his wisdom, leave orchid and mugwort undistinguished, and toil day after day following swallows and sparrows?"
translations.idiomatic: How can a great man hoard his wisdom, leave orchid, and mugwort undistinguished,, and toil day after day following swallows, and sparrows?"

sentences.zh: 」於是奏詩，義慶奇之。

translations.literal: He then submitted his poems; Yi Qing thought them extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted his poems; Yi Qing found them extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 賜帛二十匹，尋擢為國侍郎，甚見知賞。

translations.literal: He was granted twenty bolts of silk; soon he was promoted to Gentleman of the Principality and was greatly known and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted twenty bolts of silk; soon he was promoted to Gentleman of the Principality, and was greatly known, and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 遷秣陵令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Moling.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Moling.

sentences.zh: 文帝以為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen made him Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen appointed him Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上好為文章，自謂人莫能及，照悟其旨，為文章多鄙言累句。

translations.literal: The Emperor loved composing essays and considered that no man could match him; Zhao grasped his intent and in his essays used many vulgar words piled in sentences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved composing essays and considered that no man could match him; Zhao grasped his intent and in his essays used many vulgar words piled in sentences.

sentences.zh: 咸謂照才盡，實不然也。

translations.literal: All said Zhao's talent was exhausted — in fact it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone said Zhao's talent was exhausted; in fact it was not so.

sentences.zh: 臨海王子頊為荊州，照為前軍參軍，掌書記之任。

translations.literal: Prince Zishang of Linhai was in Jingzhou; Zhao was Forward Army Major and held the duty of secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zishang of Linhai held Jingzhou; Zhao served as forward army major and held the duty of secretary.

sentences.zh: 子頊敗，為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: When Zishang was defeated, he was killed by mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zishang was defeated, he was killed by mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 子澄之，升明末貴達。

translations.literal: His son Chengzhi, in the late Shengming era, rose to high rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengzhi. in the late Shengming era, rose to high rank.

sentences.zh: 澄之弟琨之為竟陵王誕司空主簿。

translations.literal: Chengzhi's younger brother Kunzhi was Chief Clerk to Prince Dan of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi's younger brother Kunzhi was chief clerk to Prince Dan of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 誕有寶琴，左右犯其徽，誕罰焉。

translations.literal: Dan had a precious zither; a attendant touched its bridge and Dan punished him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had a precious zither; an attendant touched its bridge and Dan punished him.

sentences.zh: 琨之諫，誕曰：「此餘寶也。

translations.literal: Kunzhi remonstrated; Dan said, "This is my leftover treasure."
translations.idiomatic: Kunzhi remonstrated, but Dan replied, "This is my leftover treasure."

sentences.zh: 」琨之曰：「前哲以善人為寶，不以珠玉為寶，故王孫圉稱觀父為楚國之寶。

translations.literal: Kunzhi said, "Former sages took good men as treasure, not pearls and jade as treasure — therefore Wang Sunyu called Guan Zhong the treasure of the state of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Kunzhi said, "Former sages took good men as treasure, not pearls and jade — therefore Wang Sunyu called Guan Zhong the treasure of Chu.

sentences.zh: 未聞以琴瑟為寶。

translations.literal: I have never heard of taking zithers and lutes as treasure."
translations.idiomatic: I have never heard of taking zithers, and lutes as treasure."

sentences.zh: 」誕忸然不悅。

translations.literal: Dan was ashamed and displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was ashamed, and displeased.

sentences.zh: 誕之叛，以為中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Dan rebelled, he was made Middle Army Major.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan rebelled, Kunzhi was made middle army major.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「忠孝不得並，琨之老父在，將安之乎。

translations.literal: He declined, saying, "Loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled — Kunzhi's old father lives; where can he settle?"
translations.idiomatic: He declined, saying, "Loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled — my old father still lives; where can I settle?"

sentences.zh: 」誕殺之。

translations.literal: Dan killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan killed him.

sentences.zh: 後贈黃門郎，詔謝莊為誄。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; an edict ordered Xie Zhuang to compose the eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, he was posthumously made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; an edict ordered Xie Zhuang to compose the eulogy.

sentences.zh: 遵考從父弟思考亦官曆清顯，卒于散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Zunkao's younger cousin by the father's side, Sikao, also held offices of clear prominence and died as Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Zunkao's younger cousin on the father's side, Sikao, also held offices of clear prominence and died as Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 子季連字惠續，早曆清官。

translations.literal: His son Jilian, styled Huixu, early held clear offices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jilian, styled Huixu, early held honorable offices.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝受禪，將及誅，太宰褚彥回素善之，固請乃免。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi received the Mandate, Jilian was about to be executed; Grand Preceptor Chu Yuanhui, who had always been kind to him, strongly pleaded and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi took the throne, Jilian was about to be executed; Grand Preceptor Chu Yuanhui, who had always been kind to him, pleaded strongly and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 建武中，為平西蕭遙欣長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era he was Chief Administrator to Xiao Yaoxin, Prince of Pingxi, and Governor of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era he was chief administrator to Prince Yaoxin of Pingxi and governor of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 遙欣多招賓客，明帝甚惡之。

translations.literal: Yaoxin greatly gathered guests; Emperor Ming deeply detested this.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoxin greatly gathered guests. Emperor Ming deeply detested this.

sentences.zh: 季連有憾於遙欣，乃密表明帝言其有異跡。

translations.literal: Jilian bore a grudge against Yaoxin and secretly reported to Emperor Ming that he showed signs of disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Jilian bore a grudge against Yaoxin and secretly reported to Emperor Ming signs of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 明帝乃以遙欣為雍州刺史，而心德季連，以為益州刺史，令據遙欣上流。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming then made Yaoxin Governor of Yongzhou, yet inwardly favored Jilian and made him Governor of Yi Province, ordering him to hold the upper stream above Yaoxin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming then made Yaoxin governor of Yongzhou, yet inwardly favored Jilian and made him governor of Yi, ordering him to hold the upper stream above Yaoxin.

sentences.zh: 季連父思考，宋時為益州，雖無政績，州人猶以義故，故善待之。

translations.literal: Jilian's father Sikao had been in Yi Province in Song times; though without administrative achievement, the people of the province still treated him well out of old obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Jilian's father Sikao had governed Yi Province under Song; though without great achievement, the people still treated him well out of old obligation.

sentences.zh: 季連存問故老，見父時人吏皆泣對之。

translations.literal: Jilian inquired after the old elders; when he saw men and clerks from his father's time, all wept as they answered.
translations.idiomatic: Jilian inquired after the old elders; when he met men and clerks from his father's time, all wept as they answered.

sentences.zh: 遂甯人龔愜累世有學行，辟為府主簿。

translations.literal: There was Ning man Gong Qie of several generations' learning and conduct; Jilian recruited him as chief clerk of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Qie of Ning, a man of several generations' learning and conduct, was recruited as chief clerk of the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及聞東昏失德，稍自驕矜。

translations.literal: When he heard that Emperor Donghun had lost the Way, he gradually grew proud and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Emperor Donghun had lost the Way, he gradually grew proud, and arrogant.

sentences.zh: 性忌褊，遂嚴愎酷佷，土人始怨。

translations.literal: By nature jealous and narrow, he then became stern, obstinate, cruel, and harsh; the local people began to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous and narrow by nature, he then became stern, obstinate, cruel, and harsh; the local people began to resent him.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝平建鄴，遣左右陳建孫送季連二子及弟通直郎子深喻旨，季連受命，修還裝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jianye, he sent his attendant Chen Jiansun with Jilian's two sons and his younger brother, Regular Attendant Zishen, to explain the intent; Jilian accepted the command and prepared to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jianye, he sent attendant Chen Jiansun with Jilian's two sons and his younger brother Regular Attendant Zishen to explain the imperial intent; Jilian accepted the command and prepared to return.

sentences.zh: 武帝以西台將鄧元起為益州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor made General Deng Yuanqi of the Western Headquarters Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made General Deng Yuanqi of the Western Headquarters governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 元起，南郡人，季連為南郡時，待之素薄。

translations.literal: Yuanqi was a man of Nan commandery; when Jilian was in Nan commandery he had always treated him thinly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi came from Nan commandery; when Jilian had held Nan commandery he had always treated him coldly.

sentences.zh: 元起典簽朱道琛者，嘗為季連府都錄，無賴，季連欲殺之，逃免。

translations.literal: Yuanqi's chief clerk Zhu Daochen had once been chief recorder in Jilian's headquarters; he was a ruffian; Jilian wished to kill him and he fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi's chief clerk Zhu Daochen had once been chief recorder in Jilian's headquarters; a ruffian, he had fled when Jilian wished to kill him.

sentences.zh: 至是說元起請先使檢校緣路奉迎。

translations.literal: At this time he persuaded Yuanqi to first send men to inspect and verify along the route for the welcoming mission.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he persuaded Yuanqi to first send men to inspect and verify the welcoming mission along the route.

sentences.zh: 及至，言語不恭；

translations.literal: When they arrived, their speech was disrespectful;
translations.idiomatic: Once they arrived, their speech turned disrespectful;

sentences.zh: 又曆造府州人士，見器物輒奪之，曰：「會屬人，何須苦惜」。

translations.literal: they also went about visiting men of the headquarters and prefecture; whenever they saw objects they seized them, saying, "They will soon belong to others — why begrudge them so?"
translations.idiomatic: they also went about visiting men of the headquarters, and prefecture; whenever they saw objects they seized them, saying, "They will soon belong to others; why begrudge them so?"

sentences.zh: 軍府大懼，言于季連，季連以為然。

translations.literal: The military headquarters were greatly afraid and spoke to Jilian; Jilian thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: The military headquarters were greatly afraid and spoke to Jilian; Jilian thought them right.

sentences.zh: 又惡昔之不禮元起，益憤懣。

translations.literal: He also hated his past discourtesy to Yuanqi and grew still more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: He also hated his past discourtesy to Yuanqi, and grew still more resentful.

sentences.zh: 司馬朱士略說季連求為巴西郡守，三子為質，季連許之。

translations.literal: Marshal Zhu Shilue persuaded Jilian to ask to be governor of Baxi commandery with his three sons as hostages; Jilian agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Zhu Shilue persuaded Jilian to ask to be governor of Baxi with his three sons as hostages; Jilian agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而召兵算之，精甲十萬。

translations.literal: Then he summoned troops and counted them — elite armor one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Then he summoned troops and counted them — a hundred thousand in elite armor.

sentences.zh: 臨軍歎曰：「據天嶮之地，握此盛兵，進可以匡社稷，退不失作劉備，欲以此安歸乎。

translations.literal: Facing the army he sighed and said, "Holding heaven's steep ground and grasping these mighty troops, advancing one can restore the altars, retreating one need not fail to be another Liu Bei — with this, where can I safely go?"
translations.idiomatic: Facing the army he sighed and said, "Holding heaven's steep ground and grasping these mighty troops, advancing I can restore the altars, retreating I need not fail to be another Liu Bei — with this in hand, where can I safely go?"

sentences.zh: 」遂矯稱齊宣德皇后令，復反，收朱道琛殺之。

translations.literal: He then falsely declared an order of Empress Xuan of Qi and rebelled again, seized Zhu Daochen and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then falsely declared an order of Empress Xuan of Qi, and rebelled again, seized Zhu Daochen, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 書報朱士略，兼召涪令李膺，並不受命。

translations.literal: He wrote to Zhu Shilue and also summoned Fucheng magistrate Li Ying; neither accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Zhu Shilue, and also summoned Fucheng magistrate Li Ying; neither accepted the command.

sentences.zh: 天監元年六月，元起至巴西，季連遣其將李奉伯拒戰，見敗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianjian, Yuanqi reached Baxi; Jilian sent his general Li Fengbo to resist; he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianjian, Yuanqi reached Baxi; Jilian sent his general Li Fengbo to resist and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 季連固守，元起圍之。

translations.literal: Jilian held firm; Yuanqi besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Jilian held firm while Yuanqi besieged him.

sentences.zh: 城中餓死者相枕，又從而相食。

translations.literal: Within the city the starved dead lay pillow to pillow; they then ate one another in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city the starved dead lay pillow to pillow; they then ate one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 二年，乃肉袒請罪。

translations.literal: In the second year he bared his torso to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: During the second year, he bared his torso to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 元起遷季連於外，俄而造焉，待之以禮。

translations.literal: Yuanqi moved Jilian outside; soon he visited him and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi moved Jilian outside; soon he visited him, and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 季連謝曰：「早知如此，豈有前日之事。

translations.literal: Jilian apologized, saying, "Had I known it would be like this, how could there have been yesterday's affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Jilian apologized, saying, "Had I known it would end like this, how could there have been yesterday's affair?"

sentences.zh: 」元起誅李奉伯，送季連還都。

translations.literal: Yuanqi executed Li Fengbo and sent Jilian back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi executed Li Fengbo, and sent Jilian back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 將發，人莫之視，唯龔愜送焉。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, no one looked at him; only Gong Qie saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, no one looked at him. only Gong Qie saw him off.

sentences.zh: 初，元起在道，懼事不集無以賞，士之至者皆許以辟命，於是受別駕、中從事檄者將二千人。

translations.literal: At first, while Yuanqi was on the road, fearing the affair would not succeed and having nothing with which to reward men, to all who came he promised appointment orders — thus nearly two thousand received orders as Vice Governor or Attendant Officer.
translations.idiomatic: At first, while Yuanqi was on the road, fearing failure and having nothing with which to reward men, he promised appointment orders to all who came — nearly two thousand received orders as vice governor or attendant officer.

sentences.zh: 季連既至，詣闕謝罪，自東掖門入，數步一稽首以至帝前。

translations.literal: When Jilian arrived, he went to the palace to beg forgiveness, entered by the East Flanking Gate, and every few steps bowed until he reached the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jilian arrived, he went to the palace to beg forgiveness, entered by the East Flanking Gate, and bowed every few steps until he reached the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝笑謂曰：「卿欲慕劉備而曾不及公孫述，豈無臥龍之臣乎。

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said to him, "You wished to emulate Liu Bei yet did not even reach Gongsun Shu — had you no Sleeping Dragon among your ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, "You wished to emulate Liu Bei yet did not even reach Gongsun Shu — had you no Sleeping Dragon among your ministers?"

sentences.zh: 」赦為庶人。

translations.literal: He was pardoned as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The court pardoned him, reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 四年，出建陽門，為蜀人藺相如所殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out the Jianyang Gate and was killed by Lin Xiangru of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: During the fourth year, he went out the Jianyang Gate, and was killed by Lin Xiangru of Shu.

sentences.zh: 季連在蜀，殺其父。

translations.literal: While in Shu, Xiangru had killed his father.
translations.idiomatic: While in Shu, Xiangru had killed Jilian's father.

sentences.zh: 變名走建鄴，至是報焉。

translations.literal: He changed his name and fled to Jianye; at this time he took revenge.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name, and fled to Jianye; at this time he took revenge.

sentences.zh: 乃面縛歸罪，帝壯而赦之。

translations.literal: He then bound himself and returned to confess guilt; the Emperor admired this and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He then bound himself and returned to confess guilt; the emperor admired this and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝七男：張夫人生少帝，孫修華生廬陵孝獻王義真，胡婕妤生文帝，王修容生彭城王義康，桓美人生江夏文獻王義恭，孫美人生南郡王義宣，呂美人生衡陽文王義季。

translations.literal: The Emperor Wu of Song had seven sons: Lady Zhang bore the Deposed Emperor; Sun Xiuhua bore Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen; Lady Hu the Jieyu bore Emperor Wen; Wang Xiurong bore Prince Yikang of Pengcheng; Lady Huan bore Prince Yigong of Jiangxia; Sun Meiren bore Prince Yixuan of Nan commandery; Lady Lu bore Prince Yiji of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song had seven sons: Lady Zhang bore the Deposed Emperor; Sun Xiuhua bore Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen; Lady Hu the Jieyu bore Emperor Wen; Wang Xiurong bore Prince Yikang of Pengcheng; Lady Huan bore Prince Yigong of Jiangxia; Sun Meiren bore Prince Yixuan of Nan commandery; Lady Lu bore Prince Yiji of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 沈田子既殺王鎮惡，王修又殺田子，兼裁減義真賜左右物。

translations.literal: After Shen Tianzi killed Wang Zhen'e, Wang Xiu killed Tianzi, and also cut back the gifts to Yizhen's attendants.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen Tianzi killed Wang Zhen'e, Wang Xiu killed Tianzi and also cut back the gifts to Yizhen's attendants.

sentences.zh: 左右怨之，因白義真曰：「鎮惡欲反，故田子殺之；

translations.literal: The attendants resented this and reported to Yizhen, saying, "Zhen'e wished to rebel, therefore Tianzi killed him;
translations.idiomatic: The attendants resented this, and reported to Yizhen, saying, "Zhen'e wished to rebel,,, and so Tianzi killed him;

sentences.zh: 修殺田子，豈又欲反也。

translations.literal: Xiu killed Tianzi — does he too wish to rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu killed Tianzi; does he too wish to rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」義真使左右劉乞殺修。

translations.literal: Yizhen sent his attendant Liu Qi to kill Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen had his attendant Liu Qi kill Xiu.

sentences.zh: 修字叔，京兆霸城人。

translations.literal: Xiu, styled Shu, was a man of Baling, Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, styled Shu, came from Baling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 初南度見桓玄，玄謂曰：「君平世吏部郎才也。

translations.literal: When he first crossed south and met Huan Xuan, Xuan said to him, "Sir, you have the talent of a Director of the Ministry of Personnel in peaceful times."
translations.idiomatic: When he first crossed south and met Huan Xuan, Xuan told him, "Sir, you have the talent of a Director of the Ministry of Personnel in peaceful times."

sentences.zh: 」修既死，人情離異。

translations.literal: After Xiu died, sentiment in the army turned alien.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu died. sentiment in the army turned alien.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣右將軍朱齡石代義真鎮關中，使義真疾歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor Wu sent Right General Zhu Lingshi to replace Yizhen in garrisoning Guanzhong and ordered Yizhen to return quickly because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sent Right General Zhu Lingshi to replace Yizhen in garrisoning Guanzhong and ordered Yizhen to return quickly because of illness.

sentences.zh: 諸將競斂財貨，方軌徐行。

translations.literal: The generals competed to gather wealth and goods and marched in close file at a slow pace.
translations.idiomatic: The generals competed to gather wealth and marched in close file at a slow pace.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍傅弘之曰：「虜騎若至，何以待之？

translations.literal: General Who Displays Might Fu Hongzhi said, "If barbarian cavalry arrive, how shall we meet them?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hongzhi, General Who Displays Might, asked, "If barbarian cavalry arrive, how shall we meet them?"

sentences.zh: 」賊追兵果至。

translations.literal: The pursuing enemy indeed arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers caught up as Hong had feared.

sentences.zh: 至青泥，大敗，義真獨逃草中。

translations.literal: At Qingni they were greatly defeated; Yizhen alone fled into the grass.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingni they were routed; Yizhen alone fled into the grass.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍段宏單騎追尋，義真識其聲，曰：「君非段中兵邪？

translations.literal: Middle Army Major Duan Hong pursued alone on horseback; Yizhen recognized his voice and said, "Are you not Major Duan?
translations.idiomatic: Middle Army Major Duan Hong pursued alone on horseback; Yizhen recognized his voice, and said, "Are you not Major Duan?

sentences.zh: 身在此。

translations.literal: I am here.
translations.idiomatic: I am here.

sentences.zh: 行矣，必不兩全，可刎身頭以南，使家公望絕。

translations.literal: Go — we cannot both survive; you may cut off my head and carry it south so my house's hope is ended."
translations.idiomatic: Go; we cannot both survive; you may cut off my head, and carry it south so my house's hope is ended."

sentences.zh: 」宏泣曰：「死生共之，下官不忍。

translations.literal: Hong wept and said, "Life and death together — this humble official cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Hong wept and said, "Life and death together — I cannot bear to leave you."

sentences.zh: 」乃束義真于背，單馬而歸。

translations.literal: He then bound Yizhen on his back and returned alone on one horse.
translations.idiomatic: He bound Yizhen on his back and returned alone on one horse.

sentences.zh: 義真謂宏曰：「丈夫不經此，何以知艱難。」

translations.literal: Yizhen said to Hong, "A man who has not passed through this cannot know hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen told Hong, "A man who has not passed through this cannot know hardship."

sentences.zh: 初，武帝未得義真審問，怒甚，克日北伐。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor Wu had not received certain word about Yizhen and was very angry, fixing a day for a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Wu had not received certain word about Yizhen and was very angry, fixing a day for a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 謝晦諫不從，及得宏啟，知義真免乃止。

translations.literal: Xie Hui remonstrated and was not followed; when Hong's report arrived and he knew Yizhen was safe, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui remonstrated in vain; when Hong's report arrived and he knew Yizhen was safe, he stopped.

sentences.zh: 義真尋為司州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Yizhen soon became Governor of Si Province, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen soon became governor of Si, with overall command.

sentences.zh: 以段宏為義真諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Duan Hong was made Counselor to Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hong was made Yizhen's counselor.

sentences.zh: 宏鮮卑人，為慕容超尚書左僕射，武帝伐廣固歸降。

translations.literal: Hong was a Xianbei; he had been Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing to Murong Chao and surrendered when the Emperor Wu attacked Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was a Xianbei; he had been Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing to Murong Chao and surrendered when Emperor Wu attacked Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 義真改揚州刺史，鎮石頭。

translations.literal: Yizhen was changed to Governor of Yangzhou and garrisoned Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was changed to governor of Yangzhou and garrisoned Shitou.

sentences.zh: 永初元年，封廬陵王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu he was enfeoffed Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: During the first year, of Yongchu he was enfeoffed Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 武帝始踐阼，義真色不悅，侍讀博士蔡茂之問其故。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu first ascended the throne, Yizhen's expression was displeased; Attendant Reader Doctor Cai Maozhi asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu first ascended the throne, Yizhen looked displeased; Attendant Reader Doctor Cai Maozhi asked the reason.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「安不忘危，何可恃也。

translations.literal: He answered, "In security do not forget danger — how can one rely on it?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In security do not forget danger; how can one rely on it?"

sentences.zh: 」明年遷司徒。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 武帝不豫，以為車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、南豫州刺史，加都督，鎮曆陽。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu was ill, he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat, and Governor of Southern Yu Province, with added overall command, garrisoning Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu fell ill, he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, governor of Southern Yu, and overall commander, garrisoning Liyang.

sentences.zh: 未之任而武帝崩。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post the Emperor Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the post Emperor Wu died.

sentences.zh: 義真聰敏，愛文義，而輕動無德業，與陳郡謝靈運、琅邪顏延之、慧琳道人並周旋異常，云：「得志日，以靈運、延之為宰相，慧琳道人為西豫州刺史」。

translations.literal: Yizhen was clever and loved literary meaning, but was light in action and without virtue or achievement; with Xie Lingyun of Chen commandery, Yan Yanzhi of Langye, and the monk Huilin he associated beyond the norm, saying, "On the day my ambition is fulfilled, I shall make Lingyun and Yanzhi chancellors and the monk Huilin Governor of Western Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was clever and loved letters, but was impulsive and without virtue or achievement; with Xie Lingyun of Chen, Yan Yanzhi of Langye, and the monk Huilin he associated beyond the norm, saying, "On the day my ambition is fulfilled, I shall make Lingyun and Yanzhi chancellors and Monk Huilin governor of Western Yu."

sentences.zh: 徐羨之等嫌義真與靈運、延之昵狎過甚，使故吏范晏戒之。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi and others disliked Yizhen's excessive intimacy with Lingyun and Yanzhi and sent a former clerk, Fan Yan, to warn him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi and others disliked Yizhen's excessive intimacy with Lingyun and Yanzhi and sent former clerk Fan Yan to warn him.

sentences.zh: 義真曰：「靈運空疏，延之隘薄，魏文雲'鮮能以名節自立'者。

translations.literal: Yizhen said, "Lingyun is empty and loose, Yanzhi narrow and thin — as Wei Wen said, 'rarely able to establish themselves by name and integrity.'
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen said, "Lingyun is empty and loose, Yanzhi narrow and thin — as Cao Pi said, 'rarely able to establish themselves by name and integrity.'

sentences.zh: 但性情所得，未能忘言於悟賞，故與遊耳。

translations.literal: But in temperament we find what we share and cannot forget words in mutual appreciation — therefore I associate with them."
translations.idiomatic: But in temperament we find what we share, and cannot forget words in mutual appreciation;,, and so I associate with them."

sentences.zh: 」將之鎮，列部伍於東府前。

translations.literal: As he was about to go to his post, he arrayed his troops before the Eastern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to go to his post. he arrayed his troops before the Eastern Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 既有國哀，義真與靈運、延之、慧琳等坐視部伍，因宴舫裏，使左右剔母舫函道施己船而取其勝者，及至曆陽，多所求索，羨之等每不盡與。

translations.literal: Though there was national mourning, Yizhen with Lingyun, Yanzhi, Huilin and others sat watching the array; then in the banquet boat they had attendants strip the covering from the mother's boat and apply it to their own to take the better parts; reaching Liyang, he made many demands, and Xianzhi and others each time did not fully grant them.
translations.idiomatic: Though there was national mourning, Yizhen with Lingyun, Yanzhi, Huilin, and others sat watching the array; then in the banquet boat they had attendants strip the covering from the mother's boat, and apply it to their own to take the better parts; reaching Liyang, he made many demands,, and Xianzhi, and others each time did not fully grant them.

sentences.zh: 深怨執政，表求還都。

translations.literal: He deeply resented those in power and memorialized asking to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply resented those in power, and memorialized asking to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，少帝之居東宮，多狎群小，謝晦嘗言于武帝曰：「陛下春秋既高，宜思存萬代。

translations.literal: At first, when the Deposed Emperor lived in the Eastern Palace, he often frolicked with lesser men; Xie Hui once spoke to the Emperor Wu, saying, "Your Majesty's years are already high — you ought to think of preserving ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the Deposed Emperor lived in the Eastern Palace, he often frolicked with lesser men; Xie Hui once spoke to Emperor Wu, saying, "Your Majesty's years are already high — you ought to think of preserving ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 神器至重，不可使負荷非才。

translations.literal: The sacred vessel is weightiest — it cannot be borne by one without talent."
translations.idiomatic: The sacred vessel is weightiest; it cannot be borne by one without talent."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「廬陵何如？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "How is Luling?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How is Luling?"

sentences.zh: 」晦曰：「臣請觀焉。

translations.literal: Hui said, "Your subject asks to observe him."
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, "Your subject asks to observe him."

sentences.zh: 」晦造義真，義真盛欲與談，晦不甚答，還曰：「德輕於才，非人主也。

translations.literal: Hui visited Yizhen; Yizhen greatly wished to converse; Hui did not greatly reply; returning he said, "Virtue lighter than talent — not a ruler of men."
translations.idiomatic: Hui visited Yizhen; Yizhen greatly wished to converse; Hui barely replied; returning he said, "Virtue lighter than talent — not a ruler of men."

sentences.zh: 」由是出居於外。

translations.literal: Because of this he was sent out to live abroad.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason he was sent to live outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 及羨之等專政，義真愈不悅。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi and others monopolized government, Yizhen grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi, and others monopolized government, Yizhen grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 時少帝失德，羨之等謀廢立，次第應在義真。

translations.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor lost the Way; Xianzhi and others plotted deposition and establishment; in order Yizhen should come next.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Deposed Emperor lost the Way; Xianzhi, and others plotted deposition, and establishment; in order Yizhen should come next.

sentences.zh: 以義真輕訬，不任主社稷，因其與少帝不協，奏廢為庶人，徙新安郡。

translations.literal: Because Yizhen was light and scornful and could not bear the altars of soil and grain, and because he was at odds with the Deposed Emperor, they memorialized deposing him as a commoner and banishing him to Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yizhen was frivolous and scornful and could not bear the altars of soil and grain, and because he was at odds with the Deposed Emperor, they memorialized deposing him as a commoner and banishing him to Xin'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 前吉陽令張約之上疏諫，徙為梁州府參軍，尋殺之。

translations.literal: Former Jiyang magistrate Zhang Yuezhi memorialized remonstrance and was banished as staff officer of Liang Province; soon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Former Jiyang magistrate Zhang Yuezhi memorialized remonstrance, and was banished as staff officer of Liang Province; soon he was killed.

sentences.zh: 景平二年，羨之等遣使殺義真於徙所，時年十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping, Xianzhi and others sent envoys to kill Yizhen at the place of banishment; he was then eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: During the second year, of Jingping, Xianzhi, and others sent envoys to kill Yizhen at the place of banishment; he was then eighteen.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年八月，詔追復先封，迎靈柩，並孫修華、謝妃一時俱還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanjia, an edict restored his former enfeoffment, welcomed the coffin, and Sun Xiuhua and Consort Xie all returned together.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanjia, an edict restored his former enfeoffment, welcomed the coffin,, and Sun Xiuhua, and Consort Xie all returned together.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，誅徐羨之、傅亮等。
