translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang and others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and others were executed.

sentences.zh: 是日，詔追崇侍中、大將軍，王如故。

translations.literal: That day an edict posthumously honored him Attendant and Grand General, prince as before.
translations.idiomatic: On that day, an edict posthumously honored him Attendant, and Grand General, prince as before.

sentences.zh: 贈張約之以郡。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuezhi was posthumously granted a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously granted Zhang Yuezhi a commandery.

sentences.zh: 義真無子，文帝以第五子紹字休胤嗣，襲廬陵王。

translations.literal: Yizhen had no son; Emperor Wen had his fifth son Shao, styled Xiuyin, succeed and inherit the Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen had no son; Emperor Wen had his fifth son Shao, styled Xiuyin, succeed, and inherit the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 紹少寬雅，位揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Shao in youth was broad and refined; he held the post of Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shao in youth was broad and refined; he held the post of governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 無子，以南平王鑠子敬先嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, Prince Shuo of Nanping's son Jingxian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, Prince Shuo of Nanping's son Jingxian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康，永初元年，封彭城王。

translations.literal: Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, in the first year of Yongchu, was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yikang of Pengcheng. in the first year of Yongchu, was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 曆南豫、南徐二州刺史，並加都督。

translations.literal: He held Southern Yu and Southern Xu as governor, both with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He held Southern Yu and Southern Xu as governor, both with overall command.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he became General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he became General of Agile Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，改授都督、荊州刺史，給班劍三十人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he was transferred to overall commander and Governor of Jingzhou, given thirty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia he was transferred to overall commander and governor of Jingzhou, given thirty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 義康少而聰察，及居方任，職事修理。

translations.literal: Yikang from youth was clever and observant; when he held frontier posts, affairs were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang from youth was clever, and observant; when he held frontier posts, affairs were well ordered.

sentences.zh: 六年，司徒王弘表義康宜還入輔。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Grand Minister of Education Wang Hong memorialized that Yikang ought to return to assist at court.
translations.idiomatic: During the sixth year, Grand Minister of Education Wang Hong memorialized that Yikang ought to return to assist at court.

sentences.zh: 徵為侍中、司徒、錄尚書事、都督、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attendant, Grand Minister of Education, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, overall commander, and Governor of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Attendant, Grand Minister of Education, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, overall commander, and governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 二府置佐領兵，與王弘共輔朝政。

translations.literal: Both headquarters set staff and led troops; with Wang Hong he jointly assisted court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Both headquarters set staff, and led troops; with Wang Hong he jointly assisted court governance.

sentences.zh: 弘既多疾，且每事推謙，自是內外眾務一斷之義康。

translations.literal: Hong had many illnesses and in each affair yielded with humility — from this all internal and external affairs were decided by Yikang alone.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had many illnesses, and in each affair yielded with humility; from this all internal, and external affairs were decided by Yikang alone.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事劉湛有經國才用，義康昔在豫州，湛為長史，既素情款，至是待遇特隆，動皆諮訪，故前後在藩多善政。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Tutor Liu Zhan had talent for governing the state; Yikang had once been in Yu Province and Zhan was Chief Administrator — their old affection was warm; now his treatment was especially lofty and every move was consulted — therefore in successive frontier posts there were many good policies.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Tutor Liu Zhan had talent for governing the state; Yikang had once been in Yu Province and Zhan was chief administrator — their old affection was warm; now his treatment was especially lofty and every move was consulted — therefore in successive frontier posts there were many good policies.

sentences.zh: 九年，王弘薨，又領揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Wang Hong died; he also headed Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the ninth year, Wang Hong died; he also headed Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年，又領太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he also headed Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: During the twelfth year, he also headed Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 義康性好吏職，銳意文案，糾剔是非，莫不精盡。

translations.literal: Yikang by nature loved clerical duties; he applied himself to documents, examined right and wrong — none were not refined to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang by nature loved clerical duties; he applied himself to documents, examined right, and wrong; none were not refined to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 既專朝權，事決自己，生殺大事，皆以錄命斷之。

translations.literal: Once he monopolized court power, affairs were decided by himself; great matters of life and death all were decided by his recorded command.
translations.idiomatic: Once he monopolized court power, affairs were decided by himself; great matters of life, and death all were decided by his recorded command.

sentences.zh: 凡所陳奏，入無不可，方伯以下，並委義康授用，由是朝野輻湊，權傾天下。

translations.literal: Whatever he memorialized, on entering none was not approved; regional governors and below — all appointments were entrusted to Yikang; because of this court and countryside gathered like wheel spokes and his power tilted the world.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he memorialized, on entering none was not approved; regional governors, and below; all appointments were entrusted to Yikang;, since of this court, and countryside gathered like wheel spokes, and his power tilted the world.

sentences.zh: 義康亦自強不息，無有懈倦。

translations.literal: Yikang also strengthened himself without ceasing; there was no slackness or weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang also strengthened himself without ceasing. there was no slackness or weariness.

sentences.zh: 府門每旦常有數百乘車，雖重定卑人微，皆被接引。

translations.literal: Every morning at the headquarters gate there were always several hundred carriages; though rank was heavy or light and men humble, all were received and led in.
translations.idiomatic: Every morning at the headquarters gate there were always several hundred carriages; though rank was heavy or light, and men humble, all were received, and led in.

sentences.zh: 又聰識過人，一聞必記，嘗所暫遇，終身不忘。

translations.literal: He was also clever and knowing beyond others — one hearing and he must remember; those he met briefly he never forgot all his life.
translations.idiomatic: He was also clever, and knowing beyond others; one hearing, and he must remember; those he met briefly he never forgot all his life.

sentences.zh: 稠人廣坐，每標題所憶，以示聰明，人物益以此推服之。

translations.literal: In dense crowds and broad seats he always marked what he recalled to display cleverness; men all the more for this submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In dense crowds, and broad seats he always marked what he recalled to display cleverness; men all the more for this submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 愛惜官爵，未嘗以階級私人。

translations.literal: He cherished official ranks and never used grades as private gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished official ranks, and never used grades as private gifts.

sentences.zh: 凡朝士有才用者，皆引入己府，自下樂為竭力，不敢欺負。

translations.literal: Whatever court gentlemen had talent and use, all were brought into his headquarters; those below gladly exerted themselves and did not dare deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever court gentlemen had talent, and use, all were brought into his headquarters; those below gladly exerted themselves, and did not dare deceive him.

sentences.zh: 文帝有虛勞疾，每意有所想，便覺心中痛裂，屬纊者相系。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen had chronic fatigue illness; whenever his mind had a thought, he felt pain splitting in his heart; those attending the sick followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had chronic fatigue illness. whenever his mind had a thought, he felt pain splitting in his heart. those attending the sick followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 義康入侍醫藥，盡心衛奉，湯藥飲食，非口所嘗不進。

translations.literal: Yikang entered to attend with medicine, exhaustively guarding and serving; soups, medicines, food and drink — what had not passed his mouth did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang entered to attend with medicine, exhaustively guarding, and serving; soups, medicines, food, and drink; what had not passed his mouth did not enter.

sentences.zh: 或連夕不寢，彌日不解衣。

translations.literal: Sometimes for successive nights he did not sleep; for whole days he did not remove his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes for successive nights he did not sleep. for whole days he did not remove his clothes.

sentences.zh: 內外眾事，皆專決施行。

translations.literal: All internal and external public affairs he decided and executed alone.
translations.idiomatic: All internal, and external public affairs he decided, and executed alone.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進位大將軍，領司徒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he advanced to Grand General and headed the Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the sixteenth year, he advanced to Grand General, and headed the Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 義康素無術學，待文義者甚薄。

translations.literal: Yikang by nature had no learning in the arts; he treated men of literary meaning very thinly.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang by nature had no learning in the arts; he treated men of letters very thinly.

sentences.zh: 袁淑嘗詣義康，義康問其年，答曰：「鄧仲華拜袞之歲。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu once called on Yikang; Yikang asked his age; he answered, "The year Deng Yu received the grand sash."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shu called on Yikang and Yikang asked his age, Shu answered, "The year Deng Yu received the grand sash."

sentences.zh: 」義康曰：「身不識也。

translations.literal: Yikang said, "I do not know him."
translations.idiomatic: Yikang replied, "I do not know the man."

sentences.zh: 」淑又曰：「陸機入洛之年。

translations.literal: Shu again said, "The year Lu Ji entered Luoyang."
translations.idiomatic: Shu added, "The year Lu Ji entered Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 」義康曰：「身不讀書，君無為作才語見向。

translations.literal: Yikang said, "I do not read books — sir, do not use talent-talk to face me."
translations.idiomatic: Yikang said, "I do not read books; sir, do not use talent-talk to face me."

sentences.zh: 」其淺陋若此。

translations.literal: He was shallow and crude like this.
translations.idiomatic: He was shallow, and crude like this.

sentences.zh: 既闇大體，自謂兄弟至親，不復存君臣形跡。

translations.literal: Once he was dark to the great pattern, he considered that as brothers of utmost closeness he need no longer preserve the forms of ruler and subject.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was dark to the great pattern, he considered that as brothers of utmost closeness he need no longer preserve the forms of ruler, and subject.

sentences.zh: 率心而行，曾無猜防。

translations.literal: He followed his heart in acting and never had suspicion or guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his heart in acting and never kept suspicion or guard.

sentences.zh: 私置僮六千餘人，不以言台。

translations.literal: He privately kept more than six thousand retainers and did not report them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He privately kept more than six thousand retainers, and did not report them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時四方獻饋，皆以上品薦義康，而以次者供禦。

translations.literal: At that time tributes from the four quarters all offered the top grade to Yikang and the next grade to the imperial table.
translations.idiomatic: Then tributes from the four quarters all offered the top grade to Yikang, and the next grade to the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 上嘗冬月噉柑，歎其形味並劣，義康在坐，曰：「今年柑殊有佳者。

translations.literal: The Emperor once in a winter month ate oranges and sighed that their form and taste were both inferior; Yikang was seated and said, "This year's oranges are especially fine."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once in winter ate oranges and sighed that their form and taste were both inferior; Yikang, seated beside him, said, "This year's oranges are especially fine."

sentences.zh: 」遣還東府取柑，大供禦者三寸。

translations.literal: He sent back to the Eastern Headquarters to fetch oranges; those supplied to the imperial table were three inches large.
translations.idiomatic: He sent back to the Eastern Headquarters to fetch oranges; those supplied to the imperial table were three inches across.

sentences.zh: 僕射殷景仁為帝所寵，與劉湛素善，而意好晚乖，湛常欲因宰輔之權傾之。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Yin Jingren was favored by the Emperor and was old friends with Liu Zhan, but their affections later diverged; Zhan always wished to use the chancellor's power to overturn him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Yin Jingren was favored by the emperor and was old friends with Liu Zhan, but their affections later diverged; Zhan always wished to use the chancellor's power to overturn him.

sentences.zh: 景仁為帝所保持，義康屢言不見用，湛愈憤。

translations.literal: Jingren was protected by the Emperor; Yikang repeatedly spoke and was not employed; Zhan grew still more angry.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren was protected by the emperor; Yikang repeatedly spoke and was not heeded; Zhan grew still more angry.

sentences.zh: 南陽劉斌，湛之宗也，有涉俗才用，為義康所知，自司徒右長史擢為左長史。

translations.literal: Liu Bin of Nanyang, of Zhan's clan, had worldly talent and use; Yikang knew him and promoted him from Right Chief Administrator of the Grand Minister of Education to Left Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin of Nanyang, of Zhan's clan, had worldly talent; Yikang knew him and promoted him from right chief administrator of the Grand Minister of Education to left chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎琅邪王履、主簿沛郡劉敬文、祭酒魯郡孔胤秀並以傾側自入，見帝疾篤，皆謂宜立長君。

translations.literal: Attendant Officer Wang Lu of Langye, Chief Clerk Liu Jingwen of Pei commandery, and Libationer Kong Yinxiu of Lu commandery all entered by leaning to one side; seeing the Emperor gravely ill, all said a grown heir ought to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Officer Wang Lu of Langye, Chief Clerk Liu Jingwen of Pei, and Libationer Kong Yinxiu of Lu all entered by leaning to one side; seeing the emperor gravely ill, all said a grown heir ought to be established.

sentences.zh: 上嘗危殆，使義康具顧命詔。

translations.literal: The Emperor was once in peril; he had Yikang draft the testamentary edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was once in peril; he had Yikang draft the testamentary edict.

sentences.zh: 義康還省，流涕以告湛及景仁。

translations.literal: Yikang returned to his office, weeping as he told Zhan and Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang returned to his office, weeping as he told Zhan, and Jingren.

sentences.zh: 湛曰：「天下艱難，詎是幼主所禦。

translations.literal: Zhan said, "The realm's hardship — how can a young lord withstand it?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said, "The realm's hardship; how can a young lord withstand it?"

sentences.zh: 」義康、景仁並不答；

translations.literal: Yikang and Jingren both did not answer;
translations.idiomatic: Yikang, and Jingren both did not answer;

sentences.zh: 而胤秀等輒就尚書儀曹索晉咸康立康帝舊事，義康不知也。

translations.literal: but Yinxiu and others at once went to the Masters of Writing Ceremonial Section to ask for the old affair of Emperor Kang's establishment in the Xianhe and Xiankang eras; Yikang did not know.
translations.idiomatic: but Yinxiu, and others at once went to the Masters of Writing Ceremonial Section to ask for the old affair of Emperor Kang's establishment in the Xianhe, and Xiankang eras; Yikang did not know.

sentences.zh: 及帝疾瘳，微聞之；

translations.literal: When the Emperor's illness recovered, he faintly heard of it;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness recovered, he faintly heard of it;

sentences.zh: 而斌等既為義康所寵，遂結朋黨，若有盡忠奉國不同己者，必構以罪黜。

translations.literal: Bin and the others, already favored by Yikang, then formed factions; if there were those who loyally served the state but differed from them, they must be framed with crimes and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, and the others, already favored by Yikang, then formed factions; if there were those who loyally served the state but differed from them, they must be framed with crimes, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 每采景仁短長，或虛造同異以告湛，自是主相之勢分矣。

translations.literal: They always gathered Jingren's faults and strengths, or falsely made differences and reported to Zhan — from this the power of ruler and chancellor divided.
translations.idiomatic: They always gathered Jingren's faults, and strengths, or falsely made differences, and reported to Zhan; from this the power of ruler, and chancellor divided.

sentences.zh: 義康欲以斌為丹陽尹，言其家貧。

translations.literal: Yikang wished to make Bin Governor of Danyang and said his family was poor.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang wished to make Bin governor of Danyang and said his family was poor.

sentences.zh: 上覺之，曰：「以為吳郡。

translations.literal: The Emperor perceived it and said, "Make him Wu commandery."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor perceived it and said, "Make him Wu commandery."

sentences.zh: 」後會稽太守羊玄保求還，義康又欲以斌代之。

translations.literal: Later Governor of Kuaiji Yang Xuanbao asked to return; Yikang again wished to replace him with Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, Governor of Kuaiji Yang Xuanbao asked to return; Yikang again wished to replace him with Bin.

sentences.zh: 上時未有所擬，倉卒曰：「我已用王鴻。

translations.literal: The Emperor at the time had not yet decided; hastily he said, "I have already used Wang Hong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at the time had not yet decided; hastily he said, "I have already used Wang Hong."

sentences.zh: 」上以嫌隙既成，將致大禍，十七年，乃收劉湛；

translations.literal: The Emperor, since rift and breach had formed and he would bring great calamity, in the seventeenth year then seized Liu Zhan;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, since rift and breach had formed and he would bring great calamity, in the seventeenth year then seized Liu Zhan;

sentences.zh: 又誅斌及大將軍錄事參軍劉敬文並賊曹孔劭秀、中兵邢懷明、主簿孔胤秀、丹陽丞孔文秀、司空從事中郎司馬亮、烏程令盛曇泰；

translations.literal: he also executed Bin and Grand General's Recorder Liu Jingwen and Criminal Section Kong Shaoxiu, Middle Army Xing Huaiming, Chief Clerk Kong Yinxiu, Danyang Assistant Kong Wenxiu, Attendant Officer of the Minister of Works Sima Liang, and Wucheng magistrate Sheng Tantai;
translations.idiomatic: he also executed Bin, and Grand General's Recorder Liu Jingwen, and Criminal Section Kong Shaoxiu, Middle Army Xing Huaiming, Chief Clerk Kong Yinxiu, Danyang Assistant Kong Wenxiu, Attendant Officer of the Minister of Works Sima Liang,, and Wucheng magistrate Sheng Tantai;

sentences.zh: 徙尚書庫部郎何默子、余姚令韓景之、永興令顏遙之、湛弟黃門郎素、斌弟給事中溫于廣州；

translations.literal: he banished Masters of Writing Storehouse Section He Mozi, Yuyao magistrate Han Jingzhi, Yongxing magistrate Yan Yaozhi, Zhan's younger brother Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Su, and Bin's younger brother Chief of Attendants Wen to Guangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: he banished Masters of Writing Storehouse Section He Mozi, Yuyao magistrate Han Jingzhi, Yongxing magistrate Yan Yaozhi, Zhan's younger brother Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Su,, and Bin's younger brother Chief of Attendants Wen to Guangzhou;

sentences.zh: 王履廢於家。

translations.literal: Wang Lu was disgraced at home.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lu was stripped of office and confined at home.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史杜驥勒兵殿內，以備非常。

translations.literal: Governor of Qingzhou Du Ji led troops inside the palace hall to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji, governor of Qingzhou, led troops into the palace hall against any surprise.

sentences.zh: 義康時入宿，留止中書省，遣人宣旨告以湛等罪。

translations.literal: Yikang was then lodging inside; he was detained at the Secretariat and men were sent to announce the crimes of Zhan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang was then lodging inside; he was detained at the Secretariat, and men were sent to announce the crimes of Zhan, and the others.

sentences.zh: 義康上表遜位，改授江州刺史，出鎮豫章，實幽之也。

translations.literal: Yikang memorialized yielding his post; he was transferred to Governor of Jiangzhou and went out to garrison Yuzhang — in fact he was confined.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang memorialized yielding his post; he was transferred to governor of Jiangzhou and sent out to garrison Yuzhang — in fact he was confined.

sentences.zh: 停省十餘日，桂陽侯義融、新渝侯義宗、秘書監徐湛之往來慰視。

translations.literal: He stopped at the Secretariat more than ten days; Marquis of Guiyang Yi Rong, Marquis of Xinyu Yi Zong, and Director of the Secretariat Xu Zhanzhi came and went to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped at the Secretariat more than ten days; Marquis of Guiyang Yi Rong, Marquis of Xinyu Yi Zong,, and Director of the Secretariat Xu Zhanzhi came, and went to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 於省奉辭，便下渚，上唯對之慟哭，遣沙門慧琳視之。

translations.literal: At the Secretariat he took leave and went down to the ford; the Emperor only faced him and wept bitterly and sent the monk Huilin to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: At the Secretariat he took leave and went down to the ford; the emperor only faced him and wept bitterly and sent Monk Huilin to visit him.

sentences.zh: 義康曰：「弟子有還理不？

translations.literal: Yikang said, "Does your disciple have reason to return?"
translations.idiomatic: Yikang asked, "Does your disciple still have grounds to return?"

sentences.zh: 」琳公曰：「恨公不讀數百卷書。

translations.literal: Huilin said, "I regret that you did not read several hundred fascicles of books."
translations.idiomatic: Huilin answered, "I regret that you did not read several hundred fascicles of books."

sentences.zh: 」征虜司馬蕭斌為義康所昵，劉斌等讒之被斥，乃以斌為諮議，領豫章太守，事無大小皆委之。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Barbarians' Major Xiao Bin was intimate with Yikang; Liu Bin and others slandered him and he was dismissed; then Bin was made Counselor and headed Yuzhang as governor — great and small affairs all were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the Barbarians' Major Xiao Bin was intimate with Yikang; Liu Bin and others slandered him and he was dismissed; then Bin was made counselor and governor of Yuzhang — great and small affairs all were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 司徒主簿謝綜素為義康所狎，以為記室。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Education Chief Clerk Xie Zong had always been familiar with Yikang and was made Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Education Chief Clerk Xie Zong had always been familiar with Yikang and was made recorder.

sentences.zh: 左右愛念者並聽隨從至豫章。

translations.literal: Attendants he loved and cherished were all allowed to follow to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants he loved, and cherished were all allowed to follow to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 辭州見許，資奉優厚，朝廷大事，皆報示之。

translations.literal: Leave from the province was granted; supplies and support were generous; great affairs of court were all reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: Leave from the province was granted; supplies, and support were generous; great affairs of court were all reported to him.

sentences.zh: 義康未敗時，東府聽事前井水忽湧，野雉江鷗併入所住齋前。

translations.literal: Before Yikang's fall, the well water before the Eastern Headquarters reception hall suddenly gushed; wild pheasants and river gulls together entered the residence before his study.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yikang's fall, the well water before the Eastern Headquarters reception hall suddenly gushed; wild pheasants, and river gulls together entered the residence before his study.

sentences.zh: 龍驤參軍巴東扶令育上表申明義康，奏，即收付建康獄賜死。

translations.literal: Dragon-Flying Major Fu Lingyu of Badong memorialized clarifying Yikang; when the memorial arrived he was seized and sent to Jiankang prison and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-Flying Major Fu Lingyu of Badong memorialized clarifying Yikang; when the memorial arrived he was seized, and sent to Jiankang prison, and granted death.

sentences.zh: 會稽長公主于兄弟為長，帝所親敬。

translations.literal: The Princess of Kuaiji was eldest among the brothers; the Emperor personally honored her.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Kuaiji was eldest among the brothers; the emperor personally honored her.

sentences.zh: 上嘗就主宴集甚歡，主起再拜頓首，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: The Emperor once went to the princess's feast and was very merry; the princess rose, bowed again and knocked her head, grief beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once went to the princess's feast and was very merry; the princess rose, bowed again and knocked her head, grief beyond control.

sentences.zh: 上不曉其意，起自扶之，主曰：「車子歲暮，必不見容，特乞其命。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not understand her intent; he rose and himself supported her; the princess said, "Chezi at year's end will surely not be spared — I specially beg his life."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not understand her intent; he rose and himself supported her; the princess said, "Chezi at year's end will surely not be spared — I specially beg his life."

sentences.zh: 」因慟哭。

translations.literal: She then wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: She then wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 上亦流涕，指蔣山曰：「必無此慮，若違今誓，便是負初寧陵。

translations.literal: The Emperor also shed tears, pointed at Mount Jiang and said, "Surely there is no such worry; if I violate today's oath, I shall have betrayed Chuning Tomb."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also shed tears, pointed at Mount Jiang and said, "Surely there is no such worry; if I violate today's oath, I shall have betrayed Chuning Tomb."

sentences.zh: 」即封所飲酒賜義康曰：「會稽姊飲憶弟，所飲余，今封送。

translations.literal: He then sealed the remaining wine he had drunk and sent it to Yikang, saying, "The Princess of Kuaiji drank remembering her younger brother — the remainder of what she drank, now sealed and sent."
translations.idiomatic: He then sealed the remaining wine he had drunk, and sent it to Yikang, saying, "The Princess of Kuaiji drank remembering her younger brother; the remainder of what she drank, now sealed, and sent."

sentences.zh: 」車子，義康小字也。

translations.literal: Chezi was Yikang's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Chezi was the childhood name of Yikang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，太子詹事范曄等謀反，事連義康，詔特宥大辟，並子女並免為庶人，絕屬籍，徙安成郡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Crown Prince Tutor Fan Ye and others plotted rebellion; the affair connected Yikang; an edict specially spared death by dismemberment — he and his sons and daughters were all reduced to commoners, cut from the register, and banished to Ancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, Crown Prince Tutor Fan Ye, and others plotted rebellion; the affair connected Yikang; an edict specially spared death by dismemberment; he, and his sons, and daughters were all reduced to commoners, cut from the register,, and banished to Ancheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 義康在安成讀漢書見淮南厲王長事，廢書歎曰：「前代乃有此，我得罪為宜也。」

translations.literal: Yikang at Ancheng read the Book of Han and saw the affair of Prince Li of Huainan; he put down the book and sighed, "Former ages had this too — my guilt is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Yikang at Ancheng read the Book of Han, and saw the affair of Prince Li of Huainan; he put down the book, and sighed, "Former ages had this too; my guilt is fitting."

sentences.zh: 二十四年，豫章胡誕世、前吳平令袁惲等謀奉戴義康，太尉江夏王義恭奏徙義康廣州，奏可，未行，會魏軍至瓜步，天下擾動，上慮有異志者奉義康為亂，孝武時鎮彭城及尚書左僕射何尚之並言宜早為之所。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Hu Danshi of Yuzhang and former Wu magistrate Yuan Yun and others plotted to install Yikang; Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia memorialized banishing Yikang to Guangzhou; the memorial was approved; before it was carried out, Wei troops reached Guabu and the realm was disturbed; the Emperor feared men of different intent would install Yikang to make trouble — Emperor Xiaowu at Pengcheng and Left Vice Director He Shangzhi both said he ought early to be dealt with.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, Hu Danshi of Yuzhang and former Wu magistrate Yuan Yun and others plotted to install Yikang; Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia memorialized banishing Yikang to Guangzhou; the memorial was approved; before it was carried out, Wei troops reached Guabu and the realm was disturbed; the emperor feared men of different intent would install Yikang to make trouble — Emperor Xiaowu at Pengcheng and Left Vice Director He Shangzhi both said he ought early to be dealt with.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，遣中書舍人嚴麝持藥賜死。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year, Attendant of the Secretariat Yan She was sent bearing medicine to grant death.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year, Yan She, Attendant of the Secretariat, was sent with poison to grant death.

sentences.zh: 義康不肯服藥，曰：「佛教自殺不復人身。

translations.literal: Yikang refused to take the medicine and said, "In Buddhism, suicide means no rebirth as a human body.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang refused to take the medicine, and said, "In Buddhism, suicide means no rebirth as a human body.

sentences.zh: 」乃以被掩殺之，以侯禮葬安成郡。

translations.literal: He was then smothered with a quilt and buried in Ancheng commandery with marquis rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was then smothered with a quilt, and buried in Ancheng commandery with marquis rites.

sentences.zh: 子允，元凶殺之。

translations.literal: His son Yun was killed by the Crown Prince the villain.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince the villain killed his son Yun.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明四年，義康女玉秀等乞反葬舊塋，詔聽之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, Yikang's daughters Yuxiu and others begged reburial in the old mound; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: During the fourth year, of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, Yikang's daughters Yuxiu, and others begged reburial in the old mound; an edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 江夏文獻王義恭，幼而明嶷，姿顏端麗，武帝特所鍾愛。

translations.literal: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, from youth bright and sharp, with dignified and beautiful appearance, was especially beloved by the Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, from youth bright and sharp, with dignified and beautiful appearance, was especially beloved by Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 帝性儉，諸子飲食不過五醆盤。

translations.literal: The Emperor by nature was frugal; the princes' food and drink did not exceed five platters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor by nature was frugal; the princes' food and drink did not exceed five platters.

sentences.zh: 義恭求須果食，日中無算，得未嘗噉，悉以與傍人。

translations.literal: Yigong asked for fruit and food; at midday there was no counting; what he got he never tasted and gave all to those beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong asked for fruit, and food; at midday there was no counting; what he got he never tasted, and gave all to those beside him.

sentences.zh: 諸王未嘗敢求，求亦不得。

translations.literal: The princes never dared ask; if they asked they did not obtain.
translations.idiomatic: The princes never dared ask. if they asked they did not obtain.

sentences.zh: 元嘉六年，為都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanjia he became overall commander and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanjia he became overall commander and governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 義恭涉獵文義，而驕奢不節。

translations.literal: Yigong ranged through literary meaning, but was proud and extravagant without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong ranged through letters, but was proud and extravagant without restraint.

sentences.zh: 及出藩，文帝與書誡之曰：

translations.literal: When he went out to the frontier, Emperor Wen wrote admonishing him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: As Yigong prepared to leave for his frontier post, Emperor Wen wrote to admonish him, saying:

sentences.zh: 禮賢下士，聖人垂訓，驕侈矜尚，先哲所去。

translations.literal: Honoring the worthy and lowering oneself to scholars — the sages left this instruction; pride, extravagance, and vainglory — the former wise removed these.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the worthy, and lowering oneself to scholars; the sages left this instruction; pride, extravagance,, and vainglory; the former wise removed these.

sentences.zh: 豁達大度，漢祖之德，猜忌褊急，魏武之累。

translations.literal: Open-mindedness and magnanimity — the virtue of Han's Founding Emperor; suspicion, narrowness, and haste — the burden of Wei Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Open-mindedness and magnanimity — the virtue of Han's Founding Emperor; suspicion, narrowness, and haste — the burden of Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 漢書稱衛青云：「大將軍遇士大夫以禮，與小人有恩。

translations.literal: The Book of Han praises Wei Qing: "The Grand General treated scholar-officials with rites and had kindness for lesser men."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han praises Wei Qing: "The Grand General treated scholar-officials with rites, and had kindness for lesser men."

sentences.zh: 」西門、安於，矯性齊美，關羽、張飛，任偏同弊。

translations.literal: Xi Men and An Yu corrected their natures to equal beauty; Guan Yu and Zhang Fei shared partiality and equal harm.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Men, and An Yu corrected their natures to equal beauty; Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei shared partiality, and equal harm.

sentences.zh: 行己舉事，深宜鑒此。

translations.literal: In conduct and action you should deeply take this as mirror.
translations.idiomatic: In conduct, and action you should deeply take this as mirror.

sentences.zh: 汝一月日自用不可過三十萬，若能省此益美。

translations.literal: Your monthly personal expense must not exceed three hundred thousand — if you can reduce this, so much the better.
translations.idiomatic: Your monthly personal expense must not exceed three hundred thousand; if you can reduce this, so much the better.

sentences.zh: 西楚殷曠，常宜早起，接對賓侶。

translations.literal: Western Chu is vast; you should often rise early and receive and answer guests.
translations.idiomatic: Western Chu is vast; you should often rise early, and receive, and answer guests.

sentences.zh: 園池堂觀，計無須改作。

translations.literal: Gardens, ponds, halls, and towers — reckon that none need rebuilding.
translations.idiomatic: Gardens, ponds, halls,, and towers; reckon that none need rebuilding.

sentences.zh: 凡訊獄前一二日，可取訊簿密與劉湛輩粗共詳論，慎無以喜怒加人。

translations.literal: For all trials, one or two days before you may take the trial register in secret and with Liu Zhan and the rest roughly discuss in detail; carefully do not add your joy or anger to men.
translations.idiomatic: For all trials, one or two days before you may take the trial register in secret, and with Liu Zhan, and the rest roughly discuss in detail; carefully do not add your joy or anger to men.

sentences.zh: 能擇善者從之，美自歸己。

translations.literal: If you can follow the good, the beauty returns to yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you can follow the good, the credit returns to yourself.

sentences.zh: 不可專意自決，以矜獨斷之明也。

translations.literal: You must not decide alone from partial intent to display the brilliance of sole judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He warned against deciding alone from partial intent merely to display the brilliance of sole judgment.

sentences.zh: 刑獄不可壅滯，一月可再訊。

translations.literal: Penal cases must not be blocked and delayed; once a month you may try again.
translations.idiomatic: Penal cases must not be blocked, and delayed; once a month you may try again.

sentences.zh: 凡事皆應慎密。

translations.literal: All affairs should be careful and secret.
translations.idiomatic: All affairs should be careful, and secret.

sentences.zh: 名器深宜慎惜，不可妄以假人。

translations.literal: Names and offices you should deeply cherish and not lightly lend to others.
translations.idiomatic: Names, and offices you should deeply cherish, and not lightly lend to others.

sentences.zh: 聲樂嬉遊，不宜令過。

translations.literal: Music, pleasure, and roaming — you should not let them exceed.
translations.idiomatic: Music, pleasure,, and roaming; you should not let them exceed.

sentences.zh: 宜數引見佐吏，非惟臣主自應相見。

translations.literal: You should often summon and meet staff officers — not only ruler and minister ought to meet each other.
translations.idiomatic: You should often summon, and meet staff officers; not only ruler, and minister ought to meet each other.

sentences.zh: 不數則彼我不親，不親無因得盡人情，人情不盡，何由具知眾事。

translations.literal: If not frequent, then he and I are not close; if not close, there is no cause to exhaust human feeling; if human feeling is not exhausted, how can one fully know the multitude of affairs?
translations.idiomatic: If not frequent, then he, and I are not close; if not close, there is no cause to exhaust human feeling; if human feeling is not exhausted, how can one fully know the multitude of affairs?

sentences.zh: 九年，為南兗州刺史，加都督，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he became Governor of Southern Yanzhou, with added overall command, garrisoning Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became governor of Southern Yanzhou, with overall command, garrisoning Guangling.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進位司空。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he advanced to Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the sixteenth year, he advanced to Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年，彭城王義康有罪出藩，征義恭為侍中、都督揚南徐兗三州、司徒、錄尚書事，領太子太傅。

translations.literal: The next year Prince Yikang of Pengcheng had guilt and went out to the frontier; Yigong was summoned as Attendant, overall commander of Yang, Southern Xu, and Yan provinces, Grand Minister of Education, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Prince Yikang of Pengcheng had guilt and went out to the frontier; Yigong was summoned as Attendant, overall commander of Yang, Southern Xu, and Yan, Grand Minister of Education, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 給班劍二十人，置佐領兵。

translations.literal: He was given twenty ceremonial swords; staff and troops were set.
translations.idiomatic: He was given twenty ceremonial swords; staff, and troops were set.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，進太尉，領司徒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he advanced to Grand Marshal and headed the Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he advanced to Grand Marshal, and headed the Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 義恭小心，且戒義康之失，雖為總錄，奉行文書而已。

translations.literal: Yigong was cautious and, warning himself against Yikang's failure, though he held overall record, he only carried out documents.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong was cautious and. warning himself against Yikang's failure, though he held overall record, he only carried out documents.

sentences.zh: 文帝安之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was reassured.
translations.idiomatic: This reassured Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 年給相府錢二千萬，他物稱此。

translations.literal: Each year the chancellor's office was given twenty million cash; other goods matched this.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the chancellor's office was given twenty million cash. other goods matched this.

sentences.zh: 而義恭性奢，用常不足，文帝又別給錢年至千萬。

translations.literal: But Yigong by nature was extravagant; his use was always insufficient; the Emperor also separately gave cash up to ten million per year.
translations.idiomatic: But Yigong by nature was extravagant; his use was always insufficient; the emperor also separately gave cash up to ten million per year.

sentences.zh: 時有獻五百里馬者，以賜義恭。

translations.literal: At that time someone presented a horse of five hundred li; it was granted to Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: Then someone presented a horse of five hundred li; it was granted to Yigong.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，文帝欲有事河、洛，義恭總統群帥，出鎮彭城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the Emperor wished to act on the Yellow and Luo rivers; Yigong commanded all the commanders and went out to garrison Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the emperor wished to act on the Yellow and Luo rivers; Yigong commanded all the commanders and went out to garrison Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 及魏軍至瓜步，義恭與孝武閉城自守。

translations.literal: When Wei troops reached Guabu, Yigong with Emperor Xiaowu closed the city and defended themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei troops reached Guabu, Yigong with Emperor Xiaowu closed the city, and defended themselves.

sentences.zh: 初，魏軍深入，上慮義恭不能固彭城，備加誡勒。

translations.literal: At first, when Wei troops penetrated deeply, the Emperor feared Yigong could not hold Pengcheng firm and added stern admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Wei troops penetrated deeply, the emperor feared Yigong could not hold Pengcheng firm and added stern admonitions.

sentences.zh: 義恭答曰：「臣雖未能臨瀚海，濟居延，庶免劉仲奔逃之恥。

translations.literal: Yigong answered, "Your subject though unable to reach the Han sea and cross Juyan, hopes at least to avoid the shame of Liu Zhong's flight."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong answered, "Your subject though unable to reach the Han sea, and cross Juyan, hopes at least to avoid the shame of Liu Zhong's flight."

sentences.zh: 」及魏軍至，義恭果欲走，賴眾議得停。

translations.literal: When Wei troops arrived, Yigong indeed wished to flee; only by the assembly's counsel was he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei troops arrived, Yigong indeed wished to flee. only by the assembly's counsel was he stopped.

sentences.zh: 降號驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His title was reduced to General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His title was reduced to General of Agile Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 魯郡孔子舊廟有柏樹二十四株，曆漢、晉，其大連抱。

translations.literal: Confucius's old temple in Lu commandery had twenty-four cypress trees; through Han and Jin their trunks were several arm-spans around.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's old temple in Lu had twenty-four cypress trees; through Han and Jin their trunks were several arm-spans around.

sentences.zh: 有二株先倒折，土人崇敬，莫之敢犯。

translations.literal: Two trees first fell and broke; the local people revered them and none dared violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Two trees first fell, and broke; the local people revered them, and none dared violate them.

sentences.zh: 義恭悉遣伐取，父老莫不歎息。

translations.literal: Yigong sent men to cut and take them all; elders sighed without end.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong sent men to cut, and take them all; elders sighed without end.

sentences.zh: 又以本官領南兗州刺史，加都督，移鎮盱眙，修館宇擬東城。

translations.literal: He also with his original office headed Southern Yanzhou, with added overall command, moved to garrison Xuyu, and built halls modeled on the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also with his original office headed Southern Yanzhou, with overall command, moved to garrison Xuyu, and built halls modeled on the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 二十九年冬，還朝，上以禦所乘蒼鷹船上迎之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-ninth year he returned to court; the Emperor with the imperial dark hawk boat went to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-ninth year he returned to court; the emperor with the imperial dark hawk boat went to meet him.

sentences.zh: 遭太妃憂，改授大將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He met the Grand Consort's mourning and was transferred to Grand General and Governor of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He met the Grand Consort's mourning and was transferred to Grand General and governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 還鎮東府。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison the Eastern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He went back to garrison the Eastern Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 元凶肆逆，其日劭急召義恭。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince the villain committed outrage, that day Shao urgently summoned Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Crown Prince the villain committed outrage, that day Shao urgently summoned Yigong.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔召太子及諸王，慮有詐妄致害者，召皆有人；

translations.literal: At first, edicts summoning the Crown Prince and the princes, fearing fraud that would bring harm, all had summoners accompany them;
translations.idiomatic: At first, edicts summoning the crown prince and the princes, fearing fraud that would bring harm, all had summoners accompany them;

sentences.zh: 至是，義恭求常所遣傳詔，劭遣之而後入。

translations.literal: at this time Yigong asked for the usual edict-bearer; Shao sent him and only then entered.
translations.idiomatic: at this time Yigong asked for the usual edict-bearer; Shao sent him, and only then entered.

sentences.zh: 義恭凡府內兵仗，並送還台。

translations.literal: Yigong altogether sent back all weapons within the headquarters to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong sent every weapon in the headquarters back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 進位太保。

translations.literal: He advanced to Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 孝武入討，劭疑義恭有異志，使入住尚書下省，分諸子並住神獸門外侍中下省。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered to suppress him, Shao suspected Yigong of a different intent and had him stay in the Lower Section of the Masters of Writing; his sons were separated to stay outside the Divine Beast Gate at the Attendants' Lower Section.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered to suppress him, Shao suspected Yigong of a different intent, and had him stay in the Lower Section of the Masters of Writing; his sons were separated to stay outside the Divine Beast Gate at the Attendants' Lower Section.

sentences.zh: 孝武前鋒至新亭，劭挾義恭出戰，故不得自拔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu's vanguard reached Xinting, Shao forced Yigong out to fight, so he could not extricate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Xiaowu's vanguard reached Xinting, Shao forced Yigong out to fight, so he could not extricate himself.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，義恭單馬南奔。

translations.literal: When defeated, Yigong fled south alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Once defeated, Yigong fled south alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 劭大怒，遣始興王浚殺義恭十二子。

translations.literal: Shao was greatly angry and sent Prince Jun of Shixing to kill Yigong's twelve sons.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was greatly angry, and sent Prince Jun of Shixing to kill Yigong's twelve sons.

sentences.zh: 義恭既至，勸孝武即位。

translations.literal: When Yigong arrived, he urged Emperor Xiaowu to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yigong arrived, he urged Emperor Xiaowu to ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 授太尉、錄尚書六條事、假黃鉞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Six Articles of the Masters of Writing, and given the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: They appointed him Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Six Articles of the Masters of Writing,, and given the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 事甯，進位太傅，領大司馬，增班劍為三十人，以在藩所服玉環大綬賜之。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he advanced to Grand Tutor, headed Grand Marshal, and his ceremonial swords were increased to thirty; the jade ring and grand sash he had worn in the frontier were granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled, he advanced to Grand Tutor, headed Grand Marshal,, and his ceremonial swords were increased to thirty; the jade ring, and grand sash he had worn in the frontier were granted to him.

sentences.zh: 上不欲致禮太傅，諷有司奏「天子不應加拜」，從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not wish to perform rites to the Grand Tutor and hinted that the authorities memorialize "the Son of Heaven ought not add bowing"; they followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish to perform rites to the Grand Tutor and hinted that the authorities memorialize "the Son of Heaven ought not add bowing"; they followed this.

sentences.zh: 及立太子，東宮文案，使先經義恭。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was established, Eastern Palace documents had first to pass through Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was established, Eastern Palace documents had first to pass through Yigong.

sentences.zh: 及南郡王義宣等反，又加黃鉞，白直百人入六門。

translations.literal: When Prince Yixuan of Nan commandery and others rebelled, the yellow battle-axe was again added and a hundred white guards entered the Six Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yixuan of Nan commandery, and others rebelled, the yellow battle-axe was again added, and a hundred white guards entered the Six Gates.

sentences.zh: 事平，以臧質七百里馬賜義恭。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Zang Zhi's seven-hundred-li horse was granted to Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: Once affairs were settled, Zang Zhi's seven-hundred-li horse was granted to Yigong.

sentences.zh: 孝武以義宣亂逆，由於強盛，欲削王侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, because Yixuan's rebellion and treason arose from excessive strength, wished to cut back princes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu,, since Yixuan's rebellion, and treason arose from excessive strength, wished to cut back princes, and marquises.

sentences.zh: 義恭希旨，請省錄尚書，上從之。

translations.literal: Yigong caught the intent and asked to reduce the Recorder of the Masters of Writing; the Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong caught the intent and asked to reduce the Recorder of the Masters of Writing; the emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 又與驃騎大將軍竟陵王誕奏陳貶損之格九條，詔外詳議。

translations.literal: He also with General of Agile Cavalry Prince Dan of Jingling memorialized nine articles of demotion and reduction; an edict ordered detailed discussion outside court.
translations.idiomatic: He also with General of Agile Cavalry Prince Dan of Jingling memorialized nine articles of demotion, and reduction; an edict ordered detailed discussion outside court.

sentences.zh: 於是有司奏九條之格猶有未盡，更加附益，凡二十四條。

translations.literal: Thereupon the authorities memorialized that the nine articles still had what was not exhausted and added further benefits — altogether twenty-four articles.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the authorities memorialized that the nine articles still had what was not exhausted, and added further benefits; altogether twenty-four articles.

sentences.zh: 大抵「聽事不得南面坐施帳；

translations.literal: Broadly: "In the reception hall one may not sit facing south with curtains spread;
translations.idiomatic: In summary: "In the reception hall one may not sit facing south with curtains spread;

sentences.zh: 國官正冬不得跣登國殿；

translations.literal: principality officials in midwinter may not ascend the principality hall barefoot;
translations.idiomatic: Midwinter rule: principality officials may not ascend the principality hall barefoot;

sentences.zh: 公主妃傳令，不得朱服；

translations.literal: princesses and consorts transmitting orders may not wear vermilion dress;
translations.idiomatic: princesses, and consorts transmitting orders may not wear vermilion dress;

sentences.zh: 輿不得重扛；

translations.literal: carriages may not have double poles;
translations.idiomatic: Carriages may not use double poles;

sentences.zh: 鄣扇不得雉尾；

translations.literal: screen-fans may not have pheasant tails;
translations.idiomatic: Screen-fans may not bear pheasant tails;

sentences.zh: 劍不得鹿盧形；

translations.literal: swords may not have deer-rut shapes;
translations.idiomatic: Swords may not take deer-rut shapes;
