translations.literal: spear pennants may not have peacock white banners;
translations.idiomatic: Spear pennants may not use peacock-white banners;

sentences.zh: 夾轂隊不得絳襖；

translations.literal: flanking escort teams may not wear crimson jackets;
translations.idiomatic: Flanking escort teams may not wear crimson jackets;

sentences.zh: 平乘但馬不得過二匹；

translations.literal: plain carriages with only horses may not exceed two horses;
translations.idiomatic: Plain horse-drawn carriages may not exceed two horses;

sentences.zh: 胡伎不得彩衣；

translations.literal: barbarian performers may not wear colored clothes;
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian performers may not wear colored clothes;

sentences.zh: 舞伎正冬著褂衣，不得莊面；

translations.literal: dancing girls in midwinter wear jacket robes and may not paint the face;
translations.idiomatic: dancing girls in midwinter wear jacket robes, and may not paint the face;

sentences.zh: 諸妃主不得著緄帶；

translations.literal: all consorts and princesses may not wear cord belts;
translations.idiomatic: all consorts, and princesses may not wear cord belts;

sentences.zh: 信幡非台省官悉用絳；

translations.literal: Xinfan banners for officials outside the Secretariat and Masters of Writing were all to use crimson;
translations.idiomatic: Signal banners for all officials outside the Secretariat and Masters of Writing were to be crimson;

sentences.zh: 郡縣內史相及封內長官于其封君，罷官則不復追敬，不稱臣；

translations.literal: commandery and district internal administrators and chancellors and frontier officials toward their enfeoffed lord — when office ends they no longer pursue reverence and do not style themselves ministers;
translations.idiomatic: commandery, and district internal administrators, and chancellors, and frontier officials toward their enfeoffed lord; when office ends they no longer pursue reverence, and do not style themselves ministers;

sentences.zh: 諸鎮常行，車前不得過六隊；

translations.literal: all garrisons on regular march — before the carriage may not exceed six teams;
translations.idiomatic: all garrisons on regular march; before the carriage may not exceed six teams;

sentences.zh: 刀不得過銀銅飾；

translations.literal: knives may not exceed silver and copper ornament;
translations.idiomatic: knives may not exceed silver, and copper ornament;

sentences.zh: 諸王女封縣主，諸王子孫襲封王之妃及封侯者夫人行，並不得鹵簿；

translations.literal: princes' daughters enfeoffed county ladies, princes' grandsons inheriting enfeoffed princes' consorts and those enfeoffed marquises' ladies on travel — all may not have halberd escort;
translations.idiomatic: princes' daughters enfeoffed county ladies, princes' grandsons inheriting enfeoffed princes' consorts, and those enfeoffed marquises' ladies on travel; all may not have halberd escort;

sentences.zh: 諸王子繼體為王者，婚葬吉凶，悉依諸國公侯之禮，不得同皇弟皇子；

translations.literal: princes' sons who succeed as kings — weddings, funerals, fortune and misfortune all follow the rites of various states' dukes and marquises and may not match imperial younger brothers and sons;
translations.idiomatic: princes' sons who succeed as kings; weddings, funerals, fortune, and misfortune all follow the rites of various states' dukes, and marquises, and may not match imperial younger brothers, and sons;

sentences.zh: 車輿非軺車不得油幢；

translations.literal: carriages that are not light carts may not have oil banners;
translations.idiomatic: Any carriage other than a light cart may not carry oil banners;

sentences.zh: 平乘船皆下兩頭作露平形，不得擬象龍舟」。

translations.literal: plain riding boats all lower both ends into exposed flat shape and may not imitate dragon boats."
translations.idiomatic: plain riding boats all lower both ends into exposed flat shape, and may not imitate dragon boats."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，為揚州刺史，加入朝不趨，贊拜不名，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he became Governor of Yangzhou, given exemption from hurrying at court audience, exemption from having his name spoken at bowing, and sword and shoes in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian he became governor of Yangzhou, given exemption from hurrying at court audience, exemption from having his name spoken at bowing, and sword and shoes in the hall.

sentences.zh: 固辭殊禮。

translations.literal: He firmly declined special rites.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly declined the special honors.

sentences.zh: 義恭撰要記五卷，起前漢訖晉太元，表上之。

translations.literal: Yigong compiled Essential Records in five fascicles, from Former Han through Jin Taixuan, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong compiled Essential Records in five fascicles, from Former Han through Jin Taixuan,, and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 詔付秘閣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it deposited in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the work deposited in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 時西陽王子尚有盛寵，義恭解揚州以避之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Zishang of Xiyang had flourishing favor; Yigong resigned Yangzhou to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Then Prince Zishang of Xiyang had flourishing favor; Yigong resigned Yangzhou to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 乃進位太宰，領司徒。

translations.literal: He then advanced to Grand Preceptor and headed the Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced to Grand Preceptor, and headed the Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 義恭常慮為孝武所疑，及海陵王休茂於襄陽為亂，乃上表稱「諸王貴重，不應居邊。

translations.literal: Yigong always feared Emperor Xiaowu's suspicion; when Prince Xiumao of Hailing rebelled at Xiangyang, he memorialized, saying, "The princes are weighty and ought not dwell on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong always feared Emperor Xiaowu's suspicion; when Prince Xiumao of Hailing rebelled at Xiangyang, he memorialized, saying, "The princes are weighty, and ought not dwell on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 有州不須置府」。

translations.literal: Where there is a province, there need be no headquarters set."
translations.idiomatic: Where a prince held a province, he need not also maintain a full headquarters staff."

sentences.zh: 其餘制度又多所減省。

translations.literal: The rest of the institutions also had many reductions and economizations.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the institutions also had many reductions, and economizations.

sentences.zh: 時孝武嚴暴，義恭慮不見容，乃卑辭曲意附會，皆有容儀，每有祥瑞輒上賦頌。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu was stern and violent; Yigong feared he would not be tolerated and therefore used humble words and bent intent to attach himself — all had proper bearing; whenever there were auspicious omens he submitted odes of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Xiaowu was stern, and violent; Yigong feared he would not be tolerated and,, and so used humble words, and bent intent to attach himself; all had proper bearing; whenever there were auspicious omens he submitted odes of praise.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，有三脊茅生石頭西岸，又勸封禪，上甚悅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming, three-ridge thatch grew on the west bank of Shitou; he also urged enfeoffment and feng and shan sacrifices; the Emperor was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming, three-ridge thatch grew on the west bank of Shitou; he also urged enfeoffment and feng and shan sacrifices; the emperor was very pleased.

sentences.zh: 及孝武崩，遺詔：「義恭解尚書令，加中書監。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, the testamentary edict: "Yigong is relieved of Director of the Masters of Writing and given added Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, the testamentary edict: "Yigong is relieved of Director of the Masters of Writing, and given added Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 柳元景領尚書令，入住城內。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjing heads the Masters of Writing and enters to dwell within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing heads the Masters of Writing, and enters to dwell within the city.

sentences.zh: 事無巨細，悉關二公，大事與沈慶之參決，若有軍旅，可為總統。

translations.literal: Affairs great and small all pass to the two lords; great affairs are jointly decided with Shen Qingzhi; if there are military affairs, he may be overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs great, and small all pass to the two lords; great affairs are jointly decided with Shen Qingzhi; if there are military affairs, he may be overall commander.

sentences.zh: 尚書中事委顏師伯，外監所統委王玄謨。」

translations.literal: Masters of Writing internal affairs are entrusted to Yan Shibo; outer supervision commanded affairs are entrusted to Wang Xuanmo."
translations.idiomatic: Internal affairs of the Masters of Writing were entrusted to Yan Shibo; commanded affairs of outer supervision went to Wang Xuanmo."

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，復錄尚書，本官如故。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, he again recorded the Masters of Writing; his original offices were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Former Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, he again recorded the Masters of Writing. his original offices were as before.

sentences.zh: 尚書令柳元景即本號開府儀同三司，領兵置佐，一依舊准。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Yuanjing with his original title opened an office equal to the Three Excellencies, led troops and set staff — all followed the old standard.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Yuanjing with his original title opened an office equal to the Three Excellencies, led troops, and set staff; all followed the old standard.

sentences.zh: 又增義恭班劍為四十人，更申殊禮之命。

translations.literal: Yigong's ceremonial swords were again increased to forty; special rites were again declared.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong's ceremonial swords were again increased to forty. special rites were again declared.

sentences.zh: 固辭殊禮。

translations.literal: He firmly declined special rites.
translations.idiomatic: Again he firmly declined the special honors.

sentences.zh: 義恭性嗜不恒，與時移變，自始至終，屢遷第宅。

translations.literal: Yigong's tastes by nature were not constant and shifted with the times; from beginning to end he repeatedly moved residences.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong's tastes by nature were not constant, and shifted with the times; from beginning to end he repeatedly moved residences.

sentences.zh: 與人遊款，意好亦多不終。

translations.literal: With men he was intimate — affections also often did not last to the end.
translations.idiomatic: With men he was intimate; affections also often did not last to the end.

sentences.zh: 奢侈無度，不愛財寶，左右親幸，一日乞與，或至一二百萬；

translations.literal: Extravagant without measure, he did not love treasure; attendants close and favored — in one day of begging and granting, sometimes one or two million;
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant without measure, he did not love treasure; attendants close, and favored; in one day of begging, and granting, sometimes one or two million;

sentences.zh: 小有忤意，輒追奪之。

translations.literal: with slight offense of intent he at once pursued and seized back.
translations.idiomatic: with slight offense of intent he at once pursued, and seized back.

sentences.zh: 大明時，資供豐厚，而用常不足。

translations.literal: In the Daming era supplies were rich and thick, yet his use was always insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era supplies were rich, and thick, yet his use was always insufficient.

sentences.zh: 賒市百姓物，無錢可還，民有通辭求錢者，輒題後作「原」字。

translations.literal: He bought on credit from common people; with no money to repay, when people pressed with excuses to ask for money he wrote "原" on the back.
translations.idiomatic: He bought on credit from common people; with no money to repay, when people pressed with excuses to ask for money he wrote "forgiven" on the back.

sentences.zh: 善騎馬，解音律，遊行或二三百里，孝武恣其所之。

translations.literal: Skilled at riding horses and understanding music and pitch, in roaming he sometimes went two or three hundred li; Emperor Xiaowu indulged wherever he wished to go.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at riding horses, and understanding music, and pitch, in roaming he sometimes went two or three hundred li; Emperor Xiaowu indulged wherever he wished to go.

sentences.zh: 東至吳郡，登虎丘山，又登無錫縣烏山以望太湖。

translations.literal: East to Wu commandery he ascended Tiger Hill Mountain, and again ascended Wuxian's Black Mountain to view Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: East to Wu commandery he ascended Tiger Hill Mountain,, and again ascended Wuxian's Black Mountain to view Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 大明中撰國史，孝武自為義恭作傳。

translations.literal: In the Daming era he compiled the dynastic history; Emperor Xiaowu himself wrote Yigong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era he compiled the dynastic history. Emperor Xiaowu himself wrote Yigong's biography.

sentences.zh: 及永光中，雖任宰輔，而承事近臣戴法興等常若不及。

translations.literal: In the Yongguang era, though he held the chancellorship, in serving close ministers Dai Faxing and others he was always as if not reaching them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongguang era, though he held the chancellorship, in serving close ministers Dai Faxing, and others he was always as if not reaching them.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝狂悖無道，義恭、元景謀欲廢立，廢帝率羽林兵於第害之，並其四子。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor was mad and without the Way; Yigong and Yuanjing plotted to depose and establish; the Deposed Emperor led armored guards to his residence and killed him, together with his four sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor was mad, and without the Way; Yigong, and Yuanjing plotted to depose, and establish; the Deposed Emperor led armored guards to his residence, and killed him, together with his four sons.

sentences.zh: 斷析義恭支體，分裂腹胃，挑取眼睛以蜜漬之，以為鬼目粽。

translations.literal: They cut apart Yigong's limbs, split belly and stomach, picked out the eyeballs and pickled them in honey — calling them ghost-eye zongzi.
translations.idiomatic: They cut apart Yigong's limbs, split belly, and stomach, picked out the eyeballs, and pickled them in honey; calling them ghost-eye zongzi.

sentences.zh: 明帝定亂，令書「追崇侍中、都督中外諸軍、丞相，領太尉、中書監、錄尚書事、王如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming settled the disorder, an edict said, "Posthumously honor Attendant, overall commander of internal and external armies, Chancellor, heading Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, prince as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming settled the disorder, an edict said, "Posthumously honor Attendant, overall commander of internal, and external armies, Chancellor, heading Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, prince as before.

sentences.zh: 給九旒鸞輅，虎賁班劍百人，前後部羽葆、鼓吹，轀輬車」。

translations.literal: Grant nine tassels and the imperial carriage, tiger guards and ceremonial swords one hundred men, front and rear feathered banners and drum-and-pipe, and the wheeled carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Grant nine tassels, and the imperial carriage, tiger guards, and ceremonial swords one hundred men, front, and rear feathered banners, and drum-and-pipe,, and the wheeled carriage."

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，又詔陪祭廟庭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi he was again ordered to accompany sacrifice at the temple court.
translations.idiomatic: During the third year, of Taishi he was again ordered to accompany sacrifice at the temple court.

sentences.zh: 南郡王義宣，生而舌短，澀於言論。

translations.literal: Prince Yixuan of Nan commandery from birth had a short tongue and was halting in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixuan of Nan commandery from birth had a short tongue, and was halting in speech.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年，封竟陵王，都督、南兗州刺史，遷中書監，中軍將軍，給鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia he was enfeoffed Prince of Jingling, overall commander and Governor of Southern Yanzhou; he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and General of the Central Army, given drum-and-pipe.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanjia he was enfeoffed Prince of Jingling, overall commander and governor of Southern Yanzhou; he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and General of the Central Army, given drum-and-pipe.

sentences.zh: 時竟陵群蠻充斥，役刻民散，改封南譙王。

translations.literal: At that time Jingling was full of barbarian bands; corvée cut the people and scattered them; he was changed to Prince of Nanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jingling was full of barbarian bands; corvée cut the people, and scattered them; he was changed to Prince of Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 十三年，出為江州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he went out as Governor of Jiangzhou, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he went out as governor of Jiangzhou, with overall command.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝以荊州上流形勝，地廣兵強，遺詔諸子次第居之。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor Wu, because Jingzhou in the upper stream was strategically strong, with broad territory and powerful troops, in his testamentary edict ordered the sons to hold it in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Wu, because Jingzhou in the upper stream was strategically strong, with broad territory and powerful troops, in his testamentary edict ordered the sons to hold it in succession.

sentences.zh: 謝晦平後，以授彭城王義康，義康入相，次江夏王義恭，又以臨川王義慶宗室令望，且臨川烈武王有大功於社稷，義慶又居之。

translations.literal: After Xie Hui was pacified it was granted to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng; Yikang entered as chancellor; next Prince Yigong of Jiangxia; again because Prince Yiqing of Linchuan had fine reputation in the imperial clan and Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan had great merit for the altars, Yiqing also held it.
translations.idiomatic: After Xie Hui was pacified it was granted to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng; Yikang entered as chancellor; next Prince Yigong of Jiangxia; again, since Prince Yiqing of Linchuan had fine reputation in the imperial clan, and Prince Lie Wu of Linchuan had great merit for the altars, Yiqing also held it.

sentences.zh: 其後應在義宣，上以義宣人才素短，不堪居上流。

translations.literal: Afterward Yixuan should have been next; the Emperor because Yixuan's talent was by nature short and could not bear the upper stream.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Yixuan should have been next; the emperor because Yixuan's talent was by nature limited and could not bear the upper stream.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以衡陽王義季代義慶，而以義宣為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Prince Yiji of Hengyang replaced Yiqing, and Yixuan became Governor of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Prince Yiji of Hengyang replaced Yiqing, and Yixuan became governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 而會稽公主每以為言，上遲回久之。

translations.literal: But the Princess of Kuaiji always spoke on this; the Emperor hesitated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: But the Princess of Kuaiji always spoke on this; the emperor hesitated for a long time.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，乃以義宣都督七州諸軍事、車騎將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he then made Yixuan overall commander of seven provinces, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he then made Yixuan overall commander of seven provinces, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 先賜中詔曰：「師護以在西久，比表求還，出內左右，自是經國常理，亦何必其應於一往。

translations.literal: First he granted a secret edict, saying, "Shihu has been in the west long; recently he memorialized asking to return — going out and in, left and right, this is always the constant principle of governing the state; why must it answer to one going and one coming?
translations.idiomatic: First he granted a secret edict, saying, "Shihu has been in the west long; recently he memorialized asking to return; going out, and in, left, and right, this is always the constant principle of governing the state; why must it answer to one going, and one coming?

sentences.zh: 今欲聽許，以汝代之。

translations.literal: Now I wish to grant permission and have you replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to grant permission, and have you replace him.

sentences.zh: 師護雖無殊績，潔己節用，通懷期物，不恣群下。

translations.literal: Shihu though without special achievement, cleanses himself and economizes use, broadly embraces and meets things, and does not indulge the crowd below.
translations.idiomatic: Shihu though without special achievement, cleanses himself, and economizes use, broadly embraces, and meets things,, and does not indulge the crowd below.

sentences.zh: 此信未易，在彼已有次第，為士庶所安，論者乃謂未議遷之。

translations.literal: This trust is not easy; there he already has order; gentry and commoners are settled — discussants yet say relocation is not yet debated.
translations.idiomatic: This trust is not easy; there he already has order; gentry, and commoners are settled; discussants yet say relocation is not yet debated.

sentences.zh: 今之回換，更在欲為汝耳。

translations.literal: Today's rotation and exchange — more in the wish to act for you.
translations.idiomatic: Today's rotation, and exchange; more in the wish to act for you.

sentences.zh: 汝與師護年時一輩，各有其美，方物之義，亦互有少劣，若今向事脫一減之者，既於西夏交有巨礙，遷代之譏，必歸責於吾矣。

translations.literal: You and Shihu are of one generation in years; each has his beauty; in comparing things, each also has slight inferiority — if in today's affair one is reduced, then toward western Xia there is already a great barrier; the blame for rotation will surely fall on me.
translations.idiomatic: You, and Shihu are of one generation in years; each has his beauty; in comparing things, each also has slight inferiority; if in today's affair one is reduced, then toward western Xia there is already a great barrier; the blame for rotation will surely fall on me.

sentences.zh: 」師護，義季小字也。

translations.literal: Shihu was Yiji's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Shihu was the childhood name of Yiji.

sentences.zh: 義宣至鎮，勤自課厲，政事修理。

translations.literal: Yixuan reaching his post diligently examined and strengthened himself; government affairs were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan reaching his post diligently examined, and strengthened himself; government affairs were well ordered.

sentences.zh: 白皙，美鬚眉，長七尺五寸，腰帶十圍。

translations.literal: Fair-skinned, with beautiful beard and brows, seven chi five cun tall, waist belt ten arm-spans.
translations.idiomatic: Fair-skinned, with beautiful beard and brows, seven chi five cun tall, waist belt ten arm-spans around.

sentences.zh: 多畜嬪媵，後房千餘，尼媼數百，男女三十人。

translations.literal: He kept many concubines; in the rear apartments more than a thousand; Buddhist nuns several hundred; sons and daughters thirty persons.
translations.idiomatic: He kept many concubines; in the rear apartments more than a thousand; Buddhist nuns several hundred; sons, and daughters thirty persons.

sentences.zh: 崇飾綺麗，費用殷廣。

translations.literal: He adorned himself with splendor; expense was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He adorned himself, with splendor. expense was abundant.

sentences.zh: 進位司空，改侍中。

translations.literal: He advanced to Grand Minister of Works and was changed to Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Grand Minister of Works, and was changed to Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，魏軍南侵，義宣慮寇至，欲奔上明。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Wei troops invaded south; Yixuan feared the bandits would arrive and wished to flee to Shangming.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Wei troops invaded south; Yixuan feared the bandits would arrive, and wished to flee to Shangming.

sentences.zh: 及魏軍退，文帝詔之曰：「善修民務，不須營潛逃計也。

translations.literal: When Wei troops withdrew, Emperor Wen edicted him, saying, "Well cultivate the people's affairs — you need not plan secret flight."
translations.idiomatic: When Wei troops withdrew, Emperor Wen edicted him, saying, "Well cultivate the people's affairs; you need not plan secret flight."

sentences.zh: 」遷司徒、揚州刺史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Minister of Education and Governor of Yangzhou; Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Minister of Education and governor of Yangzhou; Attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，以義宣為中書監、太尉，領司徒。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince the villain murdered and established himself, he made Yixuan Director of the Secretariat, Grand Marshal, and head the Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince the villain murdered, and established himself, he made Yixuan Director of the Secretariat, Grand Marshal,, and head the Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 義宣聞之，即時起兵，征聚甲卒，傳檄近遠。

translations.literal: When Yixuan heard of it, he at once raised troops, gathered armor and soldiers, and issued proclamations near and far.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan heard of it, he at once raised troops, gathered armor, and soldiers,, and issued proclamations near, and far.

sentences.zh: 會孝武入討，義宣遣參軍徐遺寶率眾三千，助為先鋒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered to suppress him, Yixuan sent Staff Officer Xu Yibao to lead three thousand men to aid as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Xiaowu entered to suppress him, Yixuan sent Staff Officer Xu Yibao to lead three thousand men to aid as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，以義宣為中書監、都督揚豫二州、丞相、錄尚書六條事、揚州刺史，加羽葆、鼓吹，給班劍四十人，改封南郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he made Yixuan Director of the Secretariat, overall commander of Yang and Yu provinces, Chancellor, Recorder of the Six Articles of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yangzhou, given feathered banners and drum-and-pipe, forty ceremonial swords, and changed to Prince of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he made Yixuan Director of the Secretariat, overall commander of Yang and Yu, Chancellor, Recorder of the Six Articles of the Masters of Writing, and governor of Yangzhou, given feathered banners and drum-and-pipe, forty ceremonial swords, and changed to Prince of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 追諡義宣所生為獻太妃，封次子宜陽侯愷為南譙王。

translations.literal: He posthumously titled Yixuan's biological mother Consort Xian and enfeoffed second son Marquis Kai of Yiyang as Prince of Nanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously titled Yixuan's biological mother Consort Xian, and enfeoffed second son Marquis Kai of Yiyang as Prince of Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 義宣固辭內任及愷王爵。

translations.literal: Yixuan firmly declined internal appointment and Kai's princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan firmly declined internal appointment, and Kai's princely rank.

sentences.zh: 於是改授都督八州諸軍事、荊湘二州刺史，持節、侍中、丞相如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was changed to overall commander of eight provinces, Governor of Jing and Xiang provinces; holding the staff, Attendant and Chancellor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was changed to overall commander of eight provinces, governor of Jing and Xiang; holding the staff, Attendant and Chancellor as before.

sentences.zh: 降愷為宜陽縣王，將佐以下，並加賞秩。

translations.literal: Kai was reduced to Prince of Yiyang county; staff and subordinates below were all given increased ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was reduced to Prince of Yiyang county; staff, and subordinates below were all given increased ranks.

sentences.zh: 義宣在鎮十年，兵強財富。

translations.literal: Yixuan at his post ten years — troops strong, wealth abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan at his post ten years; troops strong, wealth abundant.

sentences.zh: 既首創大義，威名著天下，凡所求欲，無不必從。

translations.literal: Having first raised the great righteousness, his prestige and name filled the realm; whatever he sought and wished, none failed to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Having first raised the great righteousness, his prestige, and name filled the realm; whatever he sought, and wished, none failed to follow.

sentences.zh: 朝廷所下制度，意不同者，一不遵承。

translations.literal: Institutions sent down by court — where his intent differed, he did not follow a single one.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions sent down by court; where his intent differed, he did not follow a single one.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻孝武酒，先自酌飲，封送所餘，其不識大體如此。

translations.literal: He once presented wine to Emperor Xiaowu; he first poured and drank himself, sealed and sent the remainder — his failure to grasp the great pattern was like this.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented wine to Emperor Xiaowu; he first poured, and drank himself, sealed, and sent the remainder; his failure to grasp the great pattern was like this.

sentences.zh: 義宣移檄諸州郡，遣參軍劉諶之、尹周之等率軍下就臧質。

translations.literal: Yixuan issued proclamations to the provinces and commanderies and sent Staff Officers Liu Chenzhi, Yin Zhouzhi and others to lead troops down to join Zang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan issued proclamations to the provinces, and commanderies, and sent Staff Officers Liu Chenzhi, Yin Zhouzhi, and others to lead troops down to join Zang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史朱修之起兵奉順。

translations.literal: Governor of Yongzhou Zhu Xiuzhi raised troops to follow the legitimate cause.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi, governor of Yongzhou, raised troops for the legitimate side.

sentences.zh: 義宣率眾十萬，發自江津，舳艫數百里。

translations.literal: Yixuan led a host of one hundred thousand, set out from Jiangjin; boats and warships stretched several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan led a host of one hundred thousand, set out from Jiangjin; boats, and warships stretched several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 是日大風，船垂覆沒，僅得入中夏口。

translations.literal: That day a great wind blew; boats nearly capsized and sank; they barely entered Zhongxia Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: On that day, a great wind blew; boats nearly capsized, and sank; they barely entered Zhongxia Mouth.

sentences.zh: 以第八子慆為輔國將軍，留鎮江陵。

translations.literal: He made eighth son Tao General Who Assists the State and left him to garrison Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He made eighth son Tao General Who Assists the State, and left him to garrison Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 遣魯秀、朱曇韶萬餘人北討朱修之。

translations.literal: He sent Lu Xiu and Zhu Tanshao with more than ten thousand men north to attack Zhu Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lu Xiu, and Zhu Tanshao with more than ten thousand men north to attack Zhu Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 秀初至江陵見義宣，既出，拊膺曰：「阿兄誤人事，乃與癡人共作賊，今年敗矣。

translations.literal: When Xiu first reached Jiangling and saw Yixuan, after leaving he beat his breast and said, "Elder brother has mistaken men's affairs — to make bandits together with a fool; this year we are defeated."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu first reached Jiangling, and saw Yixuan, after leaving he beat his breast, and said, "Elder brother has mistaken men's affairs; to make bandits together with a fool; this year we are defeated."

sentences.zh: 」義宣至尋陽，與質俱下。

translations.literal: Yixuan reached Xunyang and descended together with Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan reached Xunyang, and descended together with Zhi.

sentences.zh: 質為前鋒至鵲頭，聞徐遺寶敗，魯爽於小峴授首，相視失色。

translations.literal: Zhi as vanguard reached Quetou; hearing Xu Yibao was defeated and Lu Shuang at Xiaoxian surrendered his head, they looked at each other and paled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi as vanguard reached Quetou; hearing Xu Yibao was defeated, and Lu Shuang at Xiaoxian surrendered his head, they looked at each other, and paled.

sentences.zh: 孝武使鎮北大將軍沈慶之送爽首于義宣並與書，義宣、質並駭懼。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu sent General Who Pacifies the North Shen Qingzhi to send Shuang's head to Yixuan together with a letter; Yixuan and Zhi were both terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu sent General Who Pacifies the North Shen Qingzhi to send Shuang's head to Yixuan together with a letter; Yixuan, and Zhi were both terrified.

sentences.zh: 上先遣豫州刺史王玄謨舟師頓梁山洲內，東西兩岸為卻月城，營柵甚固。

translations.literal: The Emperor first sent Governor of Yu Province Wang Xuanmo's river force to encamp inside Liangshan Isle; east and west banks were made into crescent fortresses; camp palisades were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first sent Governor of Yu Province Wang Xuanmo's river force to encamp inside Liangshan Isle; east and west banks were made into crescent fortresses; camp palisades were very strong.

sentences.zh: 撫軍柳元景據姑孰為大統，偏師鄭琨、武念戍南浦。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Army Liu Yuanjing held Gudu as grand commander; detached forces Zheng Kun and Wu Nian garrisoned Nanpu.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the Army Liu Yuanjing held Gudu as grand commander; detached forces Zheng Kun, and Wu Nian garrisoned Nanpu.

sentences.zh: 質徑入梁山，去玄謨一里許結營。

translations.literal: Zhi went straight into Liangshan and encamped one li from Xuanmo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi went straight into Liangshan, and encamped one li from Xuanmo.

sentences.zh: 義宣屯蕪湖。

translations.literal: Yixuan encamped at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan made his camp at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 五月十九日，西南風猛，質乘風順流攻玄謨西壘，冗從僕射鬍子友等戰失利，棄壘度就玄謨。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of the fifth month the southwest wind was fierce; Zhi riding the wind downstream attacked Xuanmo's western rampart; Attendant Officer Hu Ziyou and others fought and lost; they abandoned the rampart and crossed to Xuanmo.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day of the fifth month the southwest wind was fierce; Zhi riding the wind downstream attacked Xuanmo's western rampart; Attendant Officer Hu Ziyou, and others fought, and lost; they abandoned the rampart, and crossed to Xuanmo.

sentences.zh: 質又遣將龐法起數千兵趣南浦，仍使自後掩玄謨。

translations.literal: Zhi again sent General Pang Faqi with several thousand troops toward Nanpu and also had them from behind mask Xuanmo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi again sent General Pang Faqi with several thousand troops toward Nanpu, and also had them from behind mask Xuanmo.

sentences.zh: 與琨、念相遇。

translations.literal: They met Kun and Nian.
translations.idiomatic: They met Kun, and Nian.

sentences.zh: 法起戰大敗，赴水死略盡。

translations.literal: Faqi fought and was greatly defeated; those who entered the water died almost to a man.
translations.idiomatic: Faqi fought, and was greatly defeated; those who entered the water died almost to a man.

sentences.zh: 義宣至梁山，質上出軍東岸攻玄謨。

translations.literal: Yixuan reached Liangshan; Zhi above sent troops on the east bank to attack Xuanmo.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan reached Liangshan. Zhi above sent troops on the east bank to attack Xuanmo.

sentences.zh: 玄謨分遣遊擊將軍垣護之、竟陵太守薛安都等出壘奮擊，大敗質軍，軍人一時投水。

translations.literal: Xuanmo separately sent Mobile General Yuan Huzhi and Jingling Governor Xue An Du and others out of the rampart to strike fiercely; they greatly defeated Zhi's army; soldiers at once threw themselves into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo separately sent Mobile General Yuan Huzhi, and Jingling Governor Xue An Du, and others out of the rampart to strike fiercely; they greatly defeated Zhi's army; soldiers at once threw themselves into the water.

sentences.zh: 護之等因風縱火，焚其舟乘，風勢猛盛，煙爓覆江。

translations.literal: Huzhi and others then rode the wind to set fire; they burned boats and carriages; the wind's force was fierce and abundant; smoke and flames covered the river.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi, and others then rode the wind to set fire; they burned boats, and carriages; the wind's force was fierce, and abundant; smoke, and flames covered the river.

sentences.zh: 義宣時屯西岸，延火燒營殆盡。

translations.literal: Yixuan was then encamped on the west bank; spreading fire burned the camp almost to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan was then encamped on the west bank. spreading fire burned the camp almost to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 諸將乘風火之勢，縱兵攻之，眾一時奔潰。

translations.literal: The generals riding the wind and fire's momentum released troops to attack; the host at once fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The generals riding the wind, and fire's momentum released troops to attack; the host at once fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 義宣與質相失，各單舸迸走。

translations.literal: Yixuan and Zhi lost each other; each in a single skiff fled headlong.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan, and Zhi lost each other; each in a single skiff fled headlong.

sentences.zh: 東人士庶並歸順，西人與義宣相隨者，船舸猶有百餘。

translations.literal: Eastern gentry and commoners all submitted; western men who followed Yixuan still had more than a hundred boats.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern gentry, and commoners all submitted; western men who followed Yixuan still had more than a hundred boats.

sentences.zh: 女先適臧質子，過尋陽，入城取女，載以西奔。

translations.literal: His daughter had earlier married Zang Zhi's son; passing Xunyang, she entered the city to fetch her daughter and carried her west in flight.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter had earlier married Zang Zhi's son; passing Xunyang, she entered the city to fetch her daughter, and carried her west in flight.

sentences.zh: 至江夏，聞巴陵有軍被抄斷，回入徑口，步向江陵。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangxia, hearing Baling had troops who cut the route, he turned and entered Jingkou; he walked toward Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Jiangxia, hearing Baling had troops who cut the route, he turned, and entered Jingkou; he walked toward Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 眾散且盡，左右唯有十許人。

translations.literal: The host scattered and was nearly exhausted; at his side only about ten men remained.
translations.idiomatic: The host scattered, and was nearly exhausted; at his side only about ten men remained.

sentences.zh: 腳痛不復能行，就民僦露車自載。

translations.literal: Foot pain no longer allowed walking; he hired a commoner's open cart to carry himself.
translations.idiomatic: Foot pain no longer allowed walking. he hired a commoner's open cart to carry himself.

sentences.zh: 無復食，緣道求告。

translations.literal: With no food left, along the road he begged.
translations.idiomatic: With no food left. along the road he begged.

sentences.zh: 至江陵郭外，竺超人具羽儀迎之，時帶甲尚萬餘人。

translations.literal: Reaching outside Jiangling's wall, Zhu Chaoren fully prepared feathered insignia to welcome him; at the time armored men still exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching outside Jiangling's wall, Zhu Chaoren fully prepared feathered insignia to welcome him. at the time armored men still exceeded ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 義宣既入城，仍出聽事見客。

translations.literal: Yixuan having entered the city, still went out to the reception hall to see guests.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan having entered the city. still went out to the reception hall to see guests.

sentences.zh: 左右翟靈寶誡使撫慰眾賓，以「臧質違指授之宜，用致失利，今治兵繕甲，更為後圖。

translations.literal: Attendant Zhai Lingbao admonished him to comfort the many guests, saying, "Zang Zhi violated the proper command and therefore brought defeat; now we repair troops and armor for a later plan.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Zhai Lingbao admonished him to comfort the many guests, saying, "Zang Zhi violated the proper command and,, and so brought defeat; now we repair troops, and armor for a later plan.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高百敗，終成大業」。

translations.literal: Formerly Han the High had a hundred defeats yet finally achieved the great enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: He cited the old example: "Han the High suffered a hundred defeats yet finally achieved the great enterprise."

sentences.zh: 而義宣誤云：「項羽千敗」。

translations.literal: But Yixuan mistakenly said, "Xiang Yu had a thousand defeats."
translations.idiomatic: But Yixuan blundered and said, "Xiang Yu suffered a thousand defeats."

sentences.zh: 眾咸掩口而笑。

translations.literal: The crowd all covered their mouths and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Those present all covered their mouths, and laughed.

sentences.zh: 魯秀、竺超人等猶為之爪牙，欲收合餘燼，更圖一決。

translations.literal: Lu Xiu, Zhu Chaoren and others still served as his claws and teeth, wishing to gather the remaining embers and plan one final decision.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu, Zhu Chaoren, and others still served as his claws, and teeth, wishing to gather the remaining embers, and plan one final decision.

sentences.zh: 而義宣惛墊，無復神守，入內不復出，左右腹心相率奔叛。

translations.literal: But Yixuan was muddled and collapsed, no longer keeping spirit and guard; he entered within and no longer came out; attendants and trusted men one after another fled and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: But Yixuan was muddled, and collapsed, no longer keeping spirit, and guard; he entered within, and no longer came out; attendants, and trusted men one after another fled, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 魯秀北走，義宣不復自立，欲隨秀去。

translations.literal: Lu Xiu fled north; Yixuan no longer stood on his own and wished to follow Xiu away.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu fled north; Yixuan no longer stood on his own, and wished to follow Xiu away.

sentences.zh: 乃于內戎服，盛糧糗，帶背刀，攜息慆及所愛妾五人，皆著男子服相隨。

translations.literal: He then within put on military dress, loaded dried grain, carried a back knife, and took son Tao and five beloved concubines — all wearing men's dress to follow.
translations.idiomatic: He then within put on military dress, loaded dried grain, carried a back knife,, and took son Tao, and five beloved concubines; all wearing men's dress to follow.

sentences.zh: 城內擾亂，白刃交橫，義宣大懼落馬，仍便步地。

translations.literal: Within the city was disturbance; white blades crossed; Yixuan in great fear fell from his horse and then walked on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city was disturbance; white blades crossed; Yixuan in great fear fell from his horse, and then walked on the ground.

sentences.zh: 超人送城外，更以馬與之。

translations.literal: Chaoren sent him outside the wall and again gave him a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoren sent him outside the wall, and again gave him a horse.

sentences.zh: 超人還守城。

translations.literal: Chaoren returned to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoren turned back to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 義宣冀及秀，望諸將送北入魏。

translations.literal: Yixuan hoped to catch up with Xiu and looked to the generals to send him north into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan hoped to catch up with Xiu, and looked to the generals to send him north into Wei.

sentences.zh: 既失秀所在，未出郭，將士逃盡，唯餘慆及五妾兩黃門而已。

translations.literal: Having lost where Xiu was, before leaving the outer wall, officers and soldiers fled to exhaustion; only Tao and five concubines and two eunuchs remained.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost where Xiu was, before leaving the outer wall, officers, and soldiers fled to exhaustion; only Tao, and five concubines, and two eunuchs remained.

sentences.zh: 夜還向城，入南郡空廨，無床，席地至旦。

translations.literal: At night he returned toward the city, entered the empty yamen of Nan commandery; with no bed, he sat on the ground until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: At night he returned toward the city, entered the empty yamen of Nan commandery., with no bed, he sat on the ground until dawn.

sentences.zh: 遣黃門報超人，超人遣故車一乘，載送刺奸。

translations.literal: He sent a eunuch to report to Chaoren; Chaoren sent an old cart to carry and deliver him to the arrest office.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a eunuch to report to Chaoren; Chaoren sent an old cart to carry, and deliver him to the arrest office.

sentences.zh: 義宣止獄戶，坐地歎曰：「臧質老奴誤我。

translations.literal: Yixuan stopped at the prison door, sat on the ground and sighed, saying, "Old slave Zang Zhi misled me.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan stopped at the prison door, sat on the ground, and sighed, saying, "Old slave Zang Zhi misled me.

sentences.zh: 」始與五妾俱入獄，五妾尋被遣出。

translations.literal: At first he entered prison together with five concubines; the five concubines were soon sent out.
translations.idiomatic: At first he entered prison together, with five concubines. the five concubines were soon sent out.

sentences.zh: 義宣號泣語獄吏曰：「常日非苦，今日分別始是苦。

translations.literal: Yixuan wailed and wept, saying to the prison clerk, "Ordinary days were not bitter — today's parting is the bitterness."
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan wailed, and wept, saying to the prison clerk, "Ordinary days were not bitter; today's parting is the bitterness."

sentences.zh: 」大司馬江夏王義恭諸公王八座與荊州刺史朱修之書，言：「義宣反道叛恩，便宜專行大戮」。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, the various lords, and the Eight Ministers with Governor of Jingzhou Zhu Xiuzhi wrote, saying, "Yixuan has rebelled against the Way and betrayed grace — it is fitting to execute the great punishment on authority."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, the various lords,, and the Eight Ministers with Governor of Jingzhou Zhu Xiuzhi wrote, saying, "Yixuan has rebelled against the Way, and betrayed grace; it is fitting to execute the great punishment on authority."

sentences.zh: 書未達，修之已至江陵，於獄盡之。

translations.literal: The letter had not arrived when Xiuzhi had already reached Jiangling and finished him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The letter had not arrived when Xiuzhi had already reached Jiangling, and finished him in prison.

sentences.zh: 孝武聽還葬舊墓。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu granted return burial in the old tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu allowed burial in the old tomb.

sentences.zh: 長子恢年十一，拜南譙王世子。

translations.literal: Eldest son Hui, age eleven, was appointed Heir of Prince of Nanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Hui, age eleven. was appointed Heir of Prince of Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 晉氏過江，不置城門校尉及衛尉官。

translations.literal: When the Jin crossed the river, they did not set Gate Commandant of the City Gate or Minister of the Guard offices.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jin crossed the river, they did not set Gate Commandant of the City Gate or Minister of the Guard offices.

sentences.zh: 孝武欲重城禁，故復置衛尉卿，以恢為侍中，領衛尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu wished to strengthen city prohibition and therefore restored the Minister of the Guard; Hui was made Attendant and headed the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu wished to strengthen city prohibition and,, and so restored the Minister of the Guard; Hui was made Attendant, and headed the Guard.

sentences.zh: 衛尉之置，自恢始也。

translations.literal: The setting of the Guard — from Hui it began.
translations.idiomatic: The setting of the Guard; from Hui it began.

sentences.zh: 義宣反，錄付廷尉，自殺。

translations.literal: When Yixuan rebelled, he was recorded and delivered to the Court Commandant and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan rebelled, he was recorded, and delivered to the Court Commandant, and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 恢弟愷字景穆，生而養于宮中，寵均皇子。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Kai, styled Jingmu, from birth was reared in the palace; favor matched the imperial sons.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Kai, styled Jingmu, from birth was reared in the palace. favor matched the imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 十歲封宜陽侯，孝武時進為王。

translations.literal: At ten he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yiyang; under Emperor Xiaowu he advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yiyang. under Emperor Xiaowu he advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 義宣反問至，愷于尚書寺內著婦人衣，乘問訊車投臨汝公孟詡，詡於妻室內為地窟藏之。

translations.literal: When news of Yixuan's rebellion arrived, Kai within the Masters of Writing temple wore women's clothes, rode an inquiry cart and fled to Duke Meng Xu of Linru; Xu within his wife's chamber made an underground pit to hide him.
translations.idiomatic: When news of Yixuan's rebellion arrived, Kai within the Masters of Writing temple wore women's clothes, rode an inquiry cart, and fled to Duke Meng Xu of Linru; Xu within his wife's chamber made an underground pit to hide him.

sentences.zh: 事覺，並詡誅。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, both Xu were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the affair was discovered, both Xu were executed.

sentences.zh: 其餘並為修之所殺。

translations.literal: The rest were all killed by Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi killed all the rest.

sentences.zh: 衡陽文王義季，幼而夷簡，無鄙近之累。

translations.literal: Prince Wen of Hengyang, Yiji, from youth was easy and simple, without the burden of vulgar closeness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen of Hengyang, Yiji, from youth was easy, and simple, without the burden of vulgar closeness.

sentences.zh: 文帝為荊州，武帝使隨往，由是特為文帝所愛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was in Jingzhou, the Emperor Wu had him follow; because of this he was especially loved by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was in Jingzhou, Emperor Wu had him follow; because of this he was especially loved by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年，封衡陽王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia he was enfeoffed Prince of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the first year, of Yuanjia he was enfeoffed Prince of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，代臨川王義慶為都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he replaced Prince Yiqing of Linchuan as overall commander and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he replaced Prince Yiqing of Linchuan as overall commander and governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是義慶在任，遇巴、蜀擾亂，師旅應接，府庫空虛。

translations.literal: Earlier when Yiqing was in office, he met Ba and Shu in disturbance; armies responded and connected; the treasury was empty.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier when Yiqing was in office, he met Ba, and Shu in disturbance; armies responded, and connected; the treasury was empty.

sentences.zh: 義季畜財節用，數年還復充實。

translations.literal: Yiji stored wealth and economized use; within several years it again became full.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji stored wealth, and economized use; within several years it again became full.

sentences.zh: 隊主續豐母老家貧，無以充養，遂不食肉。

translations.literal: Squad leader Xu Feng's mother was old and the family poor; unable to support her, she therefore did not eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: Squad leader Xu Feng's mother was old, and the family poor; unable to support her, she,, and so did not eat meat.

sentences.zh: 義季哀其志，給豐母月米二斛，錢一千，並制豐噉肉。

translations.literal: Yiji pitied her resolve, gave Feng's mother two hu of rice per month and one thousand cash, and also ordered Feng to eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji pitied her resolve, gave Feng's mother two hu of rice per month, and one thousand cash,, and also ordered Feng to eat meat.

sentences.zh: 義季素拙書，上聽使人書啟事，唯自署名而已。

translations.literal: Yiji by nature was clumsy at writing; the Emperor permitted others to write memorials for him — he only signed his name himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji by nature was clumsy at writing; the emperor permitted others to write memorials for him — he only signed his name himself.

sentences.zh: 嘗大搜於郢，有野老帶苫而耕，命左右斥之。

translations.literal: He once held a great hunt at Ying; an old man in the fields wore straw and plowed; he ordered attendants to drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: He once held a great hunt at Ying; an old man in the fields wore straw, and plowed; he ordered attendants to drive him off.

sentences.zh: 老人擁耒對曰：「昔楚子盤遊，受譏令尹，今陽和扇氣，播厥之始，一日不作，人失其時。

translations.literal: The old man embracing his plow answered, saying, "Formerly the Chu ruler wandered in sport and received the commandant's reproach; now the warm yang fans breath — the beginning of sowing; one day without work and people lose the season.
translations.idiomatic: The old man embracing his plow answered, saying, "Formerly the Chu ruler wandered in sport, and received the commandant's reproach; now the warm yang fans breath; the beginning of sowing; one day without work, and people lose the season.

sentences.zh: 大王馳騁為樂，驅斥老夫，非勸農之意。

translations.literal: Great King gallops for pleasure and drives off this old man — this is not the intent of encouraging agriculture."
translations.idiomatic: Great King gallops for pleasure, and drives off this old man; this is not the intent of encouraging agriculture."

sentences.zh: 」義季止馬曰：「此賢者也。

translations.literal: Yiji stopped his horse and said, "This is a worthy man."
translations.idiomatic: Yiji stopped his horse, and said, "This is a worthy man."

sentences.zh: 」命賜之食。

translations.literal: He ordered food granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji ordered that food be given him.

sentences.zh: 老人曰：「籲！

translations.literal: The old man said, "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The old man exclaimed, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 願大王均其賜也。

translations.literal: I wish Great King to equalize his grant.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Great King extend the same grant to all.

sentences.zh: 苟不奪人時，則一時皆享王賜，老人不偏其私矣。

translations.literal: If you do not seize men's season, then for one season all enjoy the King's grant — the old man is not partial to private benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not seize men's season, then for one season all enjoy the King's grant; the old man is not partial to private benefit.

sentences.zh: 斯飯也弗敢當。

translations.literal: This meal I dare not accept."
translations.idiomatic: This meal I cannot accept."

sentences.zh: 」問其名，不言而退。

translations.literal: Asked his name, he did not speak and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Asked his name, he did not speak, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 義季素嗜酒，自彭城王義康廢後，遂為長夜飲，略少醒日。

translations.literal: Yiji by nature loved wine; after Prince Yikang of Pengcheng was deposed, he then made all-night drinking; slightly fewer waking days.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji by nature loved wine. after Prince Yikang of Pengcheng was deposed, he then made all-night drinking. slightly fewer waking days.

sentences.zh: 文帝詰責曰：「此非唯傷事業，亦自損性，皆汝所諳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen reproached him, saying, "This is not only harm to enterprise — it also by itself damages nature; all are what you know well.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen reproached him, saying, "This is not only harm to enterprise; it also by itself damages nature; all are what you know well.

sentences.zh: 近長沙兄弟皆緣此致故，將軍蘇征耽酒成疾，旦夕待盡。

translations.literal: Recently the Changsha brothers all because of this met their end; General Su Zheng indulged in wine and became ill, dawn and dusk awaiting extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Changsha brothers all, since of this met their end; General Su Zheng indulged in wine, and became ill, dawn, and dusk awaiting extinction.

sentences.zh: 一門無此酣法，汝于何得之？

translations.literal: One house has no such drunken method — from where did you obtain it?"
translations.idiomatic: One house has no such drunken method; from where did you obtain it?"

sentences.zh: 」義季雖奉旨，酣縱不改成疾，以至於終。

translations.literal: Yiji though he received the edict, drunken excess did not change and became illness, continuing to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji though he received the edict, drunken excess did not change, and became illness, continuing to the end.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，徵為征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、南兗州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was summoned as General Who Pacifies the North with an office equal to the Three Excellencies and Governor of Southern Yanzhou, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was summoned as General Who Pacifies the North with an office equal to the Three Excellencies and governor of Southern Yanzhou, with overall command.

sentences.zh: 發州之日，帷帳器服諸應隨刺史者，悉留之，荊楚以為美談。

translations.literal: On the day he departed the province, curtains, vessels, dress, and all that ought to follow the governor — all were left behind; Jing and Chu took this as a fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he departed the province, curtains, vessels, dress,, and all that ought to follow the governor; all were left behind; Jing, and Chu took this as a fine tale.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，魏攻邊，北州擾動。

translations.literal: The next year Wei attacked the frontier; the northern province was disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wei attacked the frontier. the northern province was disturbed.

sentences.zh: 義季慮禍，不欲以功勤自業，無他經略，唯飲酒而已。

translations.literal: Yiji feared calamity and did not wish to make merit and diligence his enterprise; he had no other strategy — only drinking wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji feared calamity, and did not wish to make merit, and diligence his enterprise; he had no other strategy; only drinking wine.

sentences.zh: 文帝又詔責之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen again edicted reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent another edict of reproach.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自古帝王之興，雖系之於歷數，至於經啟多難，莫不兼藉親賢。

translations.literal: Discussion says: From ancient times the rise of emperors and kings, though bound to the sequence of fate, when opening and bearing many hardships, none did not jointly rely on kin and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: From ancient times the rise of emperors and kings, though bound to the sequence of fate, when opening and bearing many hardships, none did not jointly rely on kin and worthies.

sentences.zh: 當於餘祅內侮，荀、桓交逼，荊楚之勢，同於累卵。

translations.literal: When remaining omens harassed within and Xun and Huan pressed from without, Jing and Chu's situation was like piled eggs.
translations.idiomatic: When remaining omens harassed within, and Xun, and Huan pressed from without, Jing, and Chu's situation was like piled eggs.

sentences.zh: 如使上略未盡，一算或遺，則得喪之機，未可知也。

translations.literal: If the upper strategy was not exhausted and one calculation was lost, then the occasion of gain and loss could not be known.
translations.idiomatic: If the upper strategy was not exhausted, and one calculation was lost, then the occasion of gain, and loss could not be known.

sentences.zh: 烈武王攬群才，揚盛策，一舉而掃勍寇，蓋亦人謀之致乎。

translations.literal: Prince Lie Wu gathered the crowd of talents and raised flourishing stratagems; in one move he swept the fierce bandits — perhaps this too was the arrival of human counsel?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lie Wu gathered the crowd of talents, and raised flourishing stratagems; in one move he swept the fierce bandits; perhaps this too was the arrival of human counsel?

sentences.zh: 長沙雖位列台鼎，不受本根之寄，跡其行事，有以知武皇之則哲。

translations.literal: Changsha though ranked among the tripods, did not receive the root's entrustment; tracing his conduct, one can know Martial Emperor's wise discrimination.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha though ranked among the tripods, did not receive the root's entrustment. tracing his conduct, one can know Martial Emperor's wise discrimination.

sentences.zh: 廬陵以帝子之重，兼高明之姿，釁跡未彰，禍生忌克，痛矣！

translations.literal: Luling with the weight of an emperor's son, together with bright and lofty bearing — before signs of offense appeared, calamity arose from jealousy and exclusion — painful!
translations.idiomatic: Luling with the weight of an emperor's son, together with bright, and lofty bearing; before signs of offense appeared, calamity arose from jealousy, and exclusion; painful!

sentences.zh: 夫天倫猶子，分形共氣，親愛之道，人理斯同；

translations.literal: Heaven's kinship is like sons; shared form and shared breath — the Way of affection, human principle is the same;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's kinship is like sons; shared form, and shared breath; the Way of affection, human principle is the same;

sentences.zh: 富貴之情，其義則舛。

translations.literal: the feeling of wealth and honor — its principle then diverges.
translations.idiomatic: the feeling of wealth, and honor; its principle then diverges.

sentences.zh: 善乎龐公之言：比之周公、管、蔡，若處茅屋之內，宜無放殺之酷。

translations.literal: Excellent is Pang Gong's word: compared to the Duke of Zhou, Guan and Cai — if dwelling within a thatched hut, surely there would be no cruelty of release and killing.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent is Pang Gong's word: compared to the Duke of Zhou, Guan, and Cai; if dwelling within a thatched hut, surely there would be no cruelty of release, and killing.

sentences.zh: 觀夫彭城、南郡，其然乎。

translations.literal: Observing Pengcheng and Nan commandery — is it not so?
translations.idiomatic: Observing Pengcheng, and Nan commandery; is it not so?

sentences.zh: 江夏地居愛子，位當上相，大明之世，親禮冠朝，屈體降身，歸於卑下，得使兩朝暴主，永無猜色，曆載踰十，以尊戚自保。

translations.literal: Jiangxia's place was the beloved son's dwelling, his rank the upper chancellor; in the Daming era, personal rites crowned the court; he bent body and lowered self, returning to the humble below — thus he enabled two generations of violent rulers forever without suspicious color; years passed more than ten, by honored kinship preserving himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxia's place was the beloved son's dwelling, his rank the upper chancellor; in the Daming era, personal rites crowned the court; he bent body, and lowered self, returning to the humble below; thus he enabled two generations of violent rulers forever without suspicious color; years passed more than ten, by honored kinship preserving himself.

sentences.zh: 及在永光，幼主南面，公旦之重，屬有所歸，自謂踐冰之慮已除，泰山之安可恃，曾未雲幾，而磔體分肌。

translations.literal: When in Yongguang the young ruler faced south, the Duke of Zhou's weight had where to return; he considered that treading-ice worry was already removed and Mount Tai's peace could be relied on — not yet how many clouds when body was quartered and flesh divided.
translations.idiomatic: When in Yongguang the young ruler faced south, the Duke of Zhou's weight had where to return; he considered that treading-ice worry was already removed, and Mount Tai's peace could be relied on; not yet how many clouds when body was quartered, and flesh divided.

sentences.zh: 古人以隱微致誡，斯為篤矣。

translations.literal: Ancient men used the hidden and subtle to deliver admonition — this is earnest indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient men used the hidden, and subtle to deliver admonition; this is earnest indeed.

sentences.zh: 衡陽晚存酒德，何先後之雲殊，其將存覆車之鑒；

translations.literal: Hengyang in his later years preserved wine virtue — why before and after so different in clouds? Perhaps he would preserve the overturned cart's mirror;
translations.idiomatic: Hengyang in his later years preserved wine virtue; why before, and after so different in clouds? Perhaps he would preserve the overturned cart's mirror;

sentences.zh: 不然，何以致於是也。

translations.literal: if not so, how did he come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how did he come to such an end?
